Get started with Gemini Apps

Create and use notebooks in Gemini Apps

Create and use notebooks in Gemini Apps

Notebooks are a way to organize your projects in Gemini Apps in a dedicated, focused space. Notebooks provide a continuous chat experience that remembers your sources, instructions, and ongoing discussions. Notebooks use both Gemini Apps and NotebookLM and share & sync info between both products.

Notebooks can be used when you want to do things like:

  • Plan a trip or vacation
  • Apply to college
  • Learn a new hobby or skill
  • Create a business plan
  • Prepare for an exam

What you need

  • To use this feature, you must be signed in to Gemini Apps with a personal Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
    • Work and school accounts are currently not supported.

Create a notebook

To create a new notebook in Gemini Apps:

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Click New notebook.
  4. Give your new notebook a name. This name helps you organize your notebooks and also helps you find the notebook in NotebookLM.
  5. Enter a prompt to start your notebook.
  6. (optional) Click sources to add files for Gemini to reference for your project.

Tips:

  • Based on your Google AI Plan, you can add up to 600 sources. Learn about NotebookLM limits.
  • Notebooks created in Gemini can’t use an existing notebook as a source.

Chat with your notebook

You can chat continuously with your notebook. Gemini remembers the context of your sources and instructions during this chat experience. Your chats in Gemini apps notebooks can include web searches and use of any Gemini tools.

Add an existing chat to a notebook

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Find the chat that you want to add to a notebook.
  4. Next to the chat, click More Add to notebook .
  5. Select the notebook you want to add the chat to.

Tip: Chats added to a notebook in Gemini Apps will automatically sync in Notebook LM.

Study notebooks

Study notebooks let you upload notes or study materials to create personalized, interactive lessons. Features include:

  • Diagnostic Quizzes: Take quizzes to identify knowledge gaps and strengths.
  • Personalized Lessons: Gemini builds bite-sized, interactive lessons based on quiz results and learning goals.
  • Progress Tracking: Lessons and recommendations automatically update as you complete activities and track your proficiency.

Tip: Study notebooks sync with NotebookLM, allowing you to create flashcards and infographics from your course materials.

Create a study notebook

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Click New notebook > Study and learn.
  4. In the conversation to set up your study notebook, tell Gemini what your learning goal is.  You can say things like:
    • Help me prep for the ACT (JEE etc)
    • Help me study for my Calculus midterm
  5. Add additional details to customize your notebook.
    • (optional) Click Add files [icon] to add study materials such as notes. You can upload files from your device or add from Google Drive.

Tips:

  • Your lessons, conversations, quizzes & tests, and uploaded sources can all be found in your study notebook. Learn how to find and manage your notebooks in Gemini Apps.
  • You can’t edit the goal of a study notebook. If you want to focus on a new goal, create a new notebook

Manage & customize notebooks

You can customize, organize, and adjust settings for your notebooks.

Find your notebooks

  1. Go to <gemini.google.com>.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Under “All Notebooks,” is a list of any notebooks you’ve created.

Tip: Any NotebookLM notebooks that you’ve shared with someone else or have been shared with you will not appear in Gemini App.

Rename a notebook

  1. Go to <gemini.google.com>.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Under “All Notebooks,” find the notebook you want to rename.
  4. Click More Rename .
  5. Enter the new name. To change the emoji, click the current emoji and select a new one.

Tip: If you rename a notebook or change the emoji in Gemini Apps, it will also be updated in NotebookLM.

Give instructions for your notebook

You can create detailed instructions for Gemini Apps, like how to format responses or the tone you want it to use.

  1. Go to <gemini.google.com>.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Under “All Notebooks,” click the notebook you want to create instructions for.
  4. At the top right, click More Notebook settings .
  5. Add the instructions for your notebook and then click Save.

Tip: Any instructions you add to a notebook in Gemini Apps will also be applied to the notebook in NotebookLM.

Pin or unpin a notebook

You can pin your frequently used notebooks for easy access.

  1. Go to <gemini.google.com>.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Under “All Notebooks,” click the notebook you want to pin.
  4. At the top right, click More Pin or Unpin .

Your pinned notebooks appear at the top of your list of notebooks in Gemini Apps.

Delete a notebook

Important:

  • If you delete a notebook in Gemini Apps it will also delete the notebook in NotebookLM.
  • If you delete a notebook, any sources or chats that you added to that notebook will also be deleted.
  1. Go to <gemini.google.com>.
  2. On the top left, click Open Sidebar .
  3. Under “All Notebooks,” click the notebook you want to delete.
  4. At the top right, click More Delete.

Add & manage sources

You can add different types of information to your notebook to provide Gemini Apps with deep context.

Supported source types
  • Files from your device: PDFs, documents, spreadsheets, images, audio,, text files, files, and .md files. .
  • Files from Google Drive.
  • Websites/URLs
  • Copied text

Tip: If you add, update, or delete a source for a notebook in Gemini apps, the source will also be added, updated, or deleted in NotebookLM.

How notebooks work with NotebookLM

Your notebook content automatically syncs between both Gemini Apps and NotebookLM. You can update your notebook in Gemini Apps or in NotebookLM.

Find & manage your recent chats in Gemini Apps

Find & manage your recent chats in Gemini Apps

You can find your recent chats in Gemini Apps. You can pin, rename, and delete your chats so the important ones are easy to find.

Important:

  • To find and manage your chats in Gemini Apps, you need to sign in to Gemini Apps. Learn how to sign in.
  • If you’re using Gemini Apps with a personal account, the features below are only available if you have Keep Activity turned on.
  • If you’re using Gemini Apps with a work or school account, your Gemini Apps Activity is controlled by your Google Workspace administrator and you can’t delete chats.

Find your pinned & recent chats

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. If your chats are hidden, at the top, click Menu .
  3. On the side panel, find your pinned and recent chats.

Search for chats

  1. If your chats are hidden, at the top, click Menu .
  2. Click Search .
  3. In the text box, enter what you want to search.
  4. Press Enter.

Pin a recent chat

  1. If your chats are hidden, at the top, click Menu .
  2. On the side panel, under “Recent,” hover over the chat you want to pin.
  3. Click More Pin .
  4. Optionally, edit the name of your chat.
  5. Click Pin. You can find your pinned chat at the top of the “Recent” section.

Unpin a chat

  1. If your chats are hidden, at the top, click Menu .
  2. On the side panel, under “Recent,” hover over the chat you want to unpin.
  3. Click More Unpin .

Rename a chat

  1. If your chats are hidden, at the top, click Menu .
  2. On the side panel, hover over the chat you want to rename.
  3. Click More Rename .

Branch a new conversation from a chat

You can create a new chat that branches off from a specific point in a conversation, then return to the main conversation to continue it.

  1. On gemini.google.com, start a chat or open a chat you want to resume.
  2. Below a response, click Menu Branch in a new chat.

Tip: Deleting a branched chat doesn’t delete the original chat. Deleting the original chat doesn’t delete a branched chat.

Ask Gemini about your past chats

Important:

  • To use this feature, you must:
    • Sign in to your personal Google Account.
    • Be 18 or older.
    • Have Keep Activity and Memory settings on.
      • Learn more about personalization with memory of your past chats.
  • For now, this feature isn’t available in Live chats. In a text chat, you can ask Gemini to reference a past Gemini Live conversation.

In a new chat, you can ask Gemini about your past Gemini chats by topic or timeframe, or ask it to reference them before responding.

Try these example prompts:

  • Summarize our discussions of the solar system.
  • What was the gift we decided on for my son’s classmate’s birthday?
How to tell if Gemini referenced your past Gemini chats

If Gemini referenced your past chats for its response, you’ll find “Previous chats” in “Sources and related content” below the response. Gemini may occasionally make mistakes and display this label incorrectly.

Delete a chat from pinned & recent chats

Important: When you delete a chat from your pinned and recent chats, it’s also deleted from Gemini Apps Activity.

  1. If your chats are hidden, at the top, click Menu .
  2. On the side panel, hover over the chat you want to delete.
  3. Click More Delete .

What happens when a chat is deleted

Important:

  • To manage Gemini Apps Activity, you need to sign in to Gemini Apps. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • This article covers Gemini Apps activity for a personal account. If you use Gemini Apps with a work or school account, your Gemini Apps Activity settings are controlled by your Google Workspace administrator. You may not be able to change your retention settings or see how long your chats are retained for Learn more about Gemini Apps activity for work and school users.

If you delete a chat in pinned and recent chats, it also deletes any content created in that chat (like Canvas docs and apps) and the related activity from Gemini Apps Activity. If data in Gemini Apps Activity is deleted, then the activity won’t appear in recent and pinned chats.

For more info, review the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice.

Gemini Apps limits & upgrades for Google AI subscribers

Gemini Apps limits & upgrades for Google AI subscribers

Notification
Starting on May 17, 2026 there will be changes to usage limits for Gemini Apps. Learn more about these changes.

Gemini Apps have compute-based usage limits that determine how much you can interact with Gemini tools and features. These limits factor in the complexity of your prompt, the models and features you use, and the length of your chat. Your limit refreshes every 5 hours until you reach your weekly limit.

You can upgrade to a Google AI plan for expanded access to features and models in Gemini Apps. Gemini Apps upgrades are part of select Google One paid plans for personal accounts. Learn more about availalble subscriptions.

Important: This article is for users managing Gemini Apps for a personal Google Account. If you’re using a work or school Google Account, learn more about using Gemini Apps with a work or school account.

  • Some features may not be available for users under the age of 18 or 13 (or the applicable age in your country). In the help center, you will find additional information about age requirements.

Gemini app access and limits

Important:

  • Gemini Apps limits may change. Access is subject to change or may be limited based on testing, experimentation, or availability.
  • Gemini Apps usage limits are designed to ensure an optimal experience for everyone. This means we may at times have to cap the number of prompts and conversations you can have, or how much you can use some features, within a specific timeframe.
Usage limits
  • Plan: Without an AI plan; Limit: Standard limits
  • Plan: AI Plus; Limit: 2x higher than standard limits
  • Plan: AI Pro; Limit: 4x higher than standard limits
  • Plan: AI Ultra; Limit: 5x or 20x higher than AI Pro limits depending on your subscription
About Gemini 3 models

Important: Model names, versions, and availability may change.

Gemini has the following available models:

  • Gemini Flash-Lite is an efficient workhorse model designed for speed. It’s ideal for everyday tasks like summarization and brainstorming.
  • Gemini Flash is a more powerful model that balances speed and reasoning to solve a large variety of problems, from simple to complex.
  • Gemini Pro is our most advanced model that excels at complex math and coding prompts with high performance and reasoning. Pro has a deeper understanding across text, files, images and videos, plus major upgrades for coding and studying. Generally, response time for Gemini 3 Pro prompts will take longer than if using other models.
Thinking level

Where available, you can adjust the thinking level for Gemini models.

  • Standard thinking is the default and best for most questions. With Standard thinking, responses will be generally faster.
  • Extended thinking is best for complex problem solving. With Extended thinking, the model will reason over your prompt longer before responding.
  • Deep think (AI Ultra only) provides maximum parallel reasoning. Deep Think queries generally can take a few minutes before seeing a response. Deep think requires the Pro model.

Tip: More advanced models and higher thinking levels consume more of your usage.

Model Access
  • Plan: Without an AI Plan; Gemini 3 Flash-lite: Yes; Gemini 3 Flash: Yes; Gemini 3 Pro: Yes
  • Plan: AI Plus; Gemini 3 Flash-lite: Yes; Gemini 3 Flash: Yes; Gemini 3 Pro: Yes
  • Plan: AI Pro; Gemini 3 Flash-lite: Yes; Gemini 3 Flash: Yes; Gemini 3 Pro: Yes
  • Plan: AI Ultra; Gemini 3 Flash-lite: Yes; Gemini 3 Flash: Yes; Gemini 3 Pro: Yes
Context windows

When you upload files to Gemini Apps, it needs to “read” the content to provide useful insights or answers. The context window is like the reading capacity. It determines how much content can be understood together at one time. A larger context window allows Gemini Apps to work with longer prompts and chats.

  • Plan: Without an AI plan; Context window: 32k tokens
  • Plan: AI Plus; Context window: 128k tokens
  • Plan: AI Pro & AI Ultra; Context window: 1 million tokens
Feature availability

Some features are only available with Google AI subscription plans. Some features (like media generation or Deep Research) will consume more of your usage.

  • Feature: Canvas
  • Feature: Gems
  • Feature: Storybook
  • Feature: Connected Apps
  • Feature: Quizzes & flashcards
  • Feature: Audio overviews
  • Feature: Screen automation
  • Feature: Slide generation
  • Feature: Deep Research
  • Feature: Daily brief
  • Feature: Gemini Spark
  • Feature: Image generation with Nano Banana 2
  • Feature: Redo images with Nano Banana Pro
  • Feature: Video generation
  • Feature: Music generation
  • Feature: Scheduled actions
  • Feature: Early access to features; Google AI Plus: Priority access to some new features

More info about limits

What you can do when you reach a usage limit

  • If you have a Google AI subscription and reach your limit, you can continue your conversation with Flash-Lite.
  • If you reach your five hour or weekly usage limits you can upgrade to a Google AI subscription with higher limits or wait until your model limit is refreshed. Learn how to upgrade.

Usage limit changes

Limits may change without notice, including due to capacity constraints. When there’s a large increase in activity in Gemini Apps, we may change limits to maintain a high standard of quality.

Important:

  • For users without a Google AI plan, some features that require more compute resources, like Deep Research, may be unavailable during periods of high demand.
  • If capacity changes, limits for users without a Google AI plan may be limited before users with a plan.

How to tell if you’re close to a limit & when it refreshes

Gemini Apps will notify you when you’re close to your limit based on your plan’s level. When you reach your limit, Gemini Apps gives you another notification that tells you when your limit will refresh.

To view your usage limits:
  1. Visit gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom left, select Settings Usage Limits .

Why you might want a larger context window

A larger context window allows Gemini to read and comprehend more. For example, with a 1M token context window, Gemini can understand up to 1,500 pages of text or 30,000 lines of code.

If you exceed the context window, this could lead to responses that don’t take into account all the content provided or miss connections or details throughout the content. This is most relevant for prompts that require attention to many details scattered throughout large files.

Guide your child’s Gemini Apps experience

Guide your child’s Gemini Apps experience

You can give your child under 13 (or the applicable age in your country) access to Gemini Apps. As a parent, you’re in control of your child’s Gemini Apps access, including turning it on or off, using the Google Family Link app.

Our filters try to limit inappropriate content from appearing, but they’re not perfect. Your child may encounter content you don’t want them to see. Like many other AI apps, Gemini is conversational and can feel like a human. It’s important for you to help your child understand that it’s an AI tool, not a person to confide in.

In this article, learn about:

  • Help your child use Gemini Apps responsibly
  • Added protections for minors in Gemini Apps
  • Gemini Apps availability for supervised accounts
  • How to manage your child’s access to Gemini Apps

Help your child use Gemini Apps responsibly

To help guide your conversations about using Gemini Apps in a responsible way, use the reminders and resources below.

Explore together

As your child is learning how to use generative AI, explore the tool with them and supervise their use.

Try Gemini Apps

Your child can use generative AI to learn and be creative. With Gemini Apps, they can do things like:

  • Ask questions about things they’re curious about, like why the sky is blue or how long dinosaurs lived.
  • Be creative by getting help writing a story, making up a silly song, or brainstorming ideas for their next art project.
  • Get a little help with learning. If they’re stuck on a tricky math problem or a book report, Gemini Apps can give them clues and explanations to help them figure it out themselves. Learn how to use Guided Learning and create study materials.

Tip: You can help your child use Gemini on your smart home devices. Learn how to guide your child’s Gemini for Home experience.

Learn about generative AI & Gemini Apps

Learn about using generative AI and responses from Gemini Apps. Here are some resources to help get started:

  • Family Guide to AI
  • Learn about generative AI
  • An overview of the Gemini app
Remember that Gemini isn’t a person

Help your child understand that although Gemini is conversational, it’s not a person and cannot think for itself or feel emotions. Its responses can sometimes seem overly encouraging or supportive. Remind them that they are interacting with an app, and Gemini should not be treated as a friend or used to discuss personal problems or secrets.

Remind your child not to enter personal information

Let your child know not to share sensitive personal information like their address, school name, or family information in their chats with Gemini Apps.

Double-check responses

Gemini is new and evolving, and can hallucinate and present inaccurate information as factual.

Help your child think critically about Gemini Apps responses.

Here are some resources to learn more about responses:

  • Learn about how AI can make mistakes
  • Learn about responses from Gemini Apps
  • View related sources
Report inappropriate or inaccurate content

Our filters try to limit access to inappropriate content, but they’re not perfect. Your child may encounter content you don’t want them to see.

If your child encounters inappropriate or incorrect content,you or your child can report it.

You can report it by submitting feedback or your child can mark it as a bad response.

Added protections for minors in Gemini Apps

Content filters

To help protect all users, Gemini Apps attempts to identify and block harmful content, avoiding certain responses that violate our policy guidelines like violence, sexually explicit material, and harassment. For more information about these types of responses, review the policy guidelines for the Gemini app.

Added content filters for minors

In addition to the protections for all Gemini Apps users, there are added content filters for minors who are signed into their Google account. These additional protections are designed to provide a more protective experience for minors, including filters to avoid Gemini claiming to be a person or having human emotions, or role-playing as a harmful character.

These filters have been designed for minors and try to limit access to inappropriate content, but they’re not perfect. Your child may encounter content you don’t want them to see.

Privacy

The Keep Activity setting is not available to users under 13 (or the applicable age in your country).

Gemini Apps availability for supervised accounts

Important: We’re gradually releasing access to Gemini Apps for supervised accounts, so access might not be available to your child just yet even if you have Gemini Apps enabled in Family Link.

Gemini Apps are not available for supervised accounts in the European Economic Area, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.

Gemini Apps feature availability for supervised accounts

Some Gemini Apps features have age requirements and are not yet available for supervised users.

Gemini as the digital assistant on Android devices

Important: “Hey Google” and Voice Match are not available to use with Gemini Apps for users under 13 (or the applicable age in your country). “Hey Google” and Voice Match will still work with other devices, like Smart Displays and smart speakers that support Google Assistant. Learn how to set up “Hey Google” and Voice Match for shared devices.

  • Google Assistant may help for certain actions. When that happens, some Google Assistant settings, like Personal Results, apply.
  • When lock screen access is turned on, Gemini can respond when the screen is locked.

Manage your child’s access to Gemini Apps

A parent must enable access before their child under 13 (or the applicable age in your country) can use Gemini Apps with a supervised account. When your child first activates the app, you’ll receive an email notification. You can change your child’s access to Gemini Apps at any time.

  1. Go to familylink.google.com or open the Family Link app .
  2. Select your child.
  3. Tap Controls Gemini Gemini Apps.
  4. Turn Gemini Apps on  or off .

Turn off a child’s access to Gemini Apps in older versions of Family Link

If you use an older version of Family Link, to turn your child’s access to Gemini Apps on or off:

  1. Go to familylink.google.com or open the Family Link app .
  2. Select your child.
  3. Tap Controls Content restrictions Gemini Gemini Apps.
  4. Turn Gemini Apps on  or off .

Troubleshoot your child’s access to Gemini Apps

If your child is unable to access Gemini Apps or gets an error message that “Gemini isn’t available for your account,” try the following steps:

  • Make sure Gemini Apps is enabled. Check your Google Family Link settings to make sure Gemini Apps is turned on. After you enable Gemini Apps in Family Link, if your child doesn’t have access yet, try restarting Gemini. It may take a few hours for the change to take effect.
  • Check if Gemini Apps is available for your child. Check that your child is trying to access Gemini Apps on an available device, or in an available language or region. Learn more about availability for users under 13 (or the applicable age in your country).

Import from other AI platforms to Gemini Apps

Import from other AI platforms to Gemini Apps

You can bring over your preferences, remembered facts & details, and general contextual information (sometimes called  “memory”) from other AI platforms. You can also choose to import your full chat history. This will allow you to continue chats that you started on another platform with Gemini Apps.

What you need

To import from another AI platform you need to:

  • Be signed in with a personal Google Account. This feature isn’t available if you sign in to a work, school, or supervised Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have access to another AI platform with your saved chats and memory.
  • Be 18 or older.

Important: This feature is currently not available in:

  • The EEA, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom.
  • Gemini in Google Messages, Gemini in Chrome, or Gemini on Android XR.

Import memory

To import memory from another AI platform:

  1. Visit gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom left, click Settings & help    Import memory to Gemini.
  3. Copy the prompt provided by Gemini Apps.
  4. Visit the AI platform you want to export from. Paste the prompt you copied into a chat or input field.
  5. Copy the response from the other AI platform that contains memories about you.
  6. Return to Gemini Apps, paste the copied response into the designated text field, and click Add memory.

After your memory is imported, Gemini Apps will create a new chat thread and integrate this content to “remember” these details for future conversations. This helps Gemini Apps understand your context better, leading to more relevant and personalized responses.

Import chat history

You can import your full chat history using a file upload method.

Important:  The time for this process will depend on the AI platform you download chats from and may take up to a day to complete.

  1. Download your chat history from the other AI platform
    • For ChatGPT:
      1. At the bottom left, click on your username.
      2. Click Settings  Data controls.
      3. Next to “Export data”, click Export Confirm Export.
    • For Claude:
      1. At the bottom left, click on your username.
      2. Click Settings  Privacy.
      3. Next to “Export data”, click Export.
      4. Select the data range you want to export and then click Export.
        • A download link will be sent to the email associated with your account on the other AI platform.
  2. Visit gemini.google.com.
  3. At the bottom left, click  Settings & help    Import memory to Gemini.
  4. Under “Import chats”, click Add.
    • The file size limit is 5 GB.
    • The supported file type is .0
  5. Find the 0 file with your exported chats and select it to start the upload process.

Tip:  You can upload up to 5 .0files per day.

View your imported chats

You can choose to delete any individual imported chats.  To delete an imported chat:

  1. Visit the Gemini web app
  2. At the top left, select Menu
  3. Under “Chats”, look for chats with the imported chat icon .

Tip: You can search your chat history to find a specific imported chat.

Delete or overwrite imported chats

You can choose to delete any individual imported chats.  To delete an imported chat:

  1. Visit the Gemini web app
  2. At the top left, select Menu
  3. Under “Chats”, find the imported chat you want to delete.
  4. Click More Delete .

Tips:

  • To delete all the imported conversations in an import, find the import entry and next to the entry, click Delete . All imported chats within that .0 file will be deleted.
  • If you reupload a  .0 file with your exported chats it will add any new conversations and overwrite previously imported ones.

Troubleshoot import issues

Understand partial imports

If an import is interrupted, you will be notified, and some chats might be partially imported. If this happens, delete the import entry and try to import again.

How your data is handled

Your imported and continued chats are saved in your Activity. This data is used to improve our services (including training generative AI models), and to protect Google, our users and the public.  You can manage or delete your activity anytime.

All imported information will be subject to the Google Privacy Policy. To understand how Google processes your data when you interact with Gemini, visit the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub.

Learn about generative AI

Learn about generative AI

Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a type of AI that can help you create content. It can help you be more creative, productive, and knowledgeable.

In this article, you can learn about generative AI, including:

  • What generative AI is and how it works
  • How to use generative AI and evaluate the accuracy of its responses
  • How Google develops AI

What is generative AI

Generative AI is a type of machine learning model. Generative AI is not a human being. It can’t think for itself or feel emotions. It’s just great at finding patterns.

In the past, AI was used to understand and recommend information. Now, generative AI can also help us create new content, like images, music, and code.

How machine learning models are trained

Machine learning models, including generative AI, learn through a process of observation and pattern matching known as training. For a model to understand what a sneaker is, it’s trained on millions of photos of sneakers. Over time, it recognizes that sneakers are objects that humans wear on their feet with laces, soles, and a logo.

The model can use training to:

  1. Take an input like “Generate an image of sneakers with a goat charm.
  2. Connect what it’s learned about sneakers, goats, and charms.
  3. Generate an image, even if it hasn’t seen an image like that before.

How Large Language Models power generative AI

Generative AI and Large Language Models (LLMs) are part of the same technology. Generative AI can be trained on any type of data, but LLMs use words as their main source of training data.

Experiences powered by LLMs, like Gemini and AI Overviews, can predict words that might come next based on your prompt and the text it’s generated so far. They’re given flexibility to pick probable next words that match patterns they get from training. This flexibility lets them generate creative responses.

If you prompt them to fill in the phrase “Harry [blank],” they might predict the next word is “Styles” or “Potter.”

How to use generative AI

Important: Google’s experiences powered by generative AI can help you start the creative process. They’re not meant to do all the work for you or be the creator.

Here are 3 ways that you can use generative AI:

  • Brainstorm your creative ideas. For example, get help writing a prequel to your favorite movie.

  • Ask questions that you didn’t think could be answered. Like, “Which came first, the chicken or the egg?”

  • Get an extra boost of help. Ask it to suggest a title for a story you’ve written, or get help identifying the species of an animal or insect in an image.

As you explore, create, and learn new things with Generative AI, it’s important to use it responsibly. For details, review our Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.

AI can & will make mistakes

Because generative AI is experimental and a work in progress, it can and will make mistakes:

  • It may make things up. When generative AI invents an answer, it’s called a hallucination. Hallucinations happen because unlike how Google Search gets information from the web, LLMs don’t gather information at all. Instead, LLMs predict which words come next based on user inputs.
    • For example, you might ask, “Who’s going to win women’s gymnastics at the 2032 Brisbane Summer Olympics?” and get a response, even though the event hasn’t happened yet.
  • It may misunderstand things. Sometimes, generative AI products misinterpret language, which changes the meaning.
    • For example, you may want to learn more about bats, the animal that lives in caves. If you ask for information about bats, it might tell you about the bats used in baseball, cricket, and softball.

Always evaluate responses

Think critically about the responses you get from generative AI tools. Use Google and other resources to check information that’s presented as fact.

If you come across something that isn’t right, report it. Many of our generative AI products have reporting tools. Your feedback helps us refine the models to improve generative AI experiences for everyone.

Use code with caution

Our generative code features are still experimental and you’re responsible for your use of suggested code or coding explanations. Please use discretion and carefully test and review all code for errors, bugs, and vulnerabilities before relying on it. Complying with any license requirements, such as where we provide citations to open source code repositories, is your responsibility. Learn more.

How Google develops AI

To make sure we build tools that make the world better for everyone, we developed a set of AI principles in 2018. These principles describe our goals to develop bold technology that can tackle some of society’s biggest challenges in a responsible way.

For example, we use AI to:

  • Support efforts to curb climate change, like reducing stop-and-go traffic to lower vehicle emissions
  • Predict or monitor natural disasters, like forecasting floods in more than 20 countries and tracking the real-time boundaries of wildfires
  • Support healthcare innovations, like making tuberculosis screening more accessible and helping with early detection of breast cancer

Our principles also list areas we won’t pursue with AI, like technologies that cause overall harm or violate international law and human rights.

Check out our full list of AI principles.

Learn in creative ways with generative AI

Learn in creative ways with generative AI

Using generative AI to uplevel your learning

Generative AI is a type of artificial intelligence (AI) that can help you learn and build new skills. It can help you learn in a way that works for you, jumpstart your creativity, and quickly assess information.

In this article, you’ll learn how generative AI can help you:

  • Prepare for tests
  • Spark inspiration
  • Quickly analyze information

Important: Make sure to check and follow your school’s policy on using Generative AI.

Prepare for tests

Generative AI can help you learn in a way that works for you. Along with reviewing your course materials, here are some ways Generative AI can help you prepare for tests:

  • Understand complex topics in creative ways: For example, “Write a rap to help me understand the trig ratios.”
  • Get step-by-step guides: For example, you can ask for detailed steps on how to solve math problems.
  • Test your knowledge: Ask for as many practice quizzes as you need to feel ready for your test.

Spark inspiration

Get a creativity boost when you’re stuck on a project or need a little inspiration. Generative AI can help you:

  • Brainstorm ideas: Ask for 3 different intros to a video series you’re recording, before writing the full script yourself. You can also ask, “Give me ten innovative science fair project ideas.”
  • Overcome writer’s block: Ask it to suggest “Five ways to start a narration for a documentary on climate change.”

You’re the creator. Generative AI is there to boost your creative process, not do all the work for you. Use its suggestions as a starting point, then add your own unique voice and ideas to create something truly original.

Quickly analyze information

You can use generative AI to quickly assess information. For example, it can help you:

  • Research important events: For example, it can help you research colleges or learn about different majors. You can ask something like, “Make a list of college majors for people who love animals.”
  • Understand different points of view: For example, you can use generative AI to help you get ready for a debate by asking it to argue for the opposing side.

Tips

  • Always evaluate responses: While generative AI is a powerful tool, it can make mistakes. It’s important to always fact-check information using built-in tools or by double-checking with Google Search.
  • Experiment: Don’t be afraid to try different prompts and see what kind of responses you get.
  • Be specific: The more specific your questions, the more helpful the AI’s answers will be.
  • Have fun! Learning should be enjoyable, and generative AI can help make it that way.

As you explore, create, and learn new things with generative AI, it’s important to use it responsibly. For details, review our Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.

You can learn more about Generative AI at ai.google.

Schedule actions in Gemini Apps

Schedule actions in Gemini Apps

You can make Gemini a part of your daily, weekly, and monthly routines by scheduling recurring actions. For example, you can schedule actions in Gemini Apps to get:

  • A daily news digest on topics that matter most to you
  • Weekly inspiration for creative projects
  • Monthly suggestions for new skills to learn

You can set a delivery time that works for your schedule. Gemini will prepare your content in the background so it’s ready by the scheduled time.

What you need

To schedule actions in Gemini Apps, you must:

  • Sign in to Gemini Apps with one of the following accounts:
    • A personal Google Account with a Google AI subscription. Learn how to upgrade.
    • A work or school Google Account with access to a qualifying edition of Google Workspace.
    • Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have Keep Activity on. This feature isn’t available when this setting is off.

Schedule an action

Important: You can have up to 10 active scheduled actions at a time.

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. In the text box at the bottom, enter your prompt. Get ideas for how to use scheduled actions.
    • Tip: In your prompt, provide details about when and how often you want to schedule the action.
  3. Click Submit . Gemini will reply with a summary of your scheduled action.
    • Gemini will prepare your content within the hour leading up to your delivery time to help ensure you get the latest information.
    • Responses for scheduled actions are prepared in advance to guarantee timely delivery. As a result, rapidly changing data, like stock prices, won’t be the latest when you receive them. Scheduled actions work best for daily summaries and wrap-ups.

Tips:

  • To update the action schedule or instructions, click More Edit. You can also ask Gemini to edit the action at any time in the scheduled action chat.
  • You can also manage and create scheduled actions in your Gemini settings. Click Settings & help Scheduled actions.
  • If you ask Gemini Apps to schedule an action that uses another app, like Google Workspace, that app must be connected. If it’s not, Gemini will ask you to connect the app. Learn how to use and manage Connected Apps in Gemini.
Examples

Here are a few examples of ways you can have Gemini help you using scheduled actions.

  • Daily digests of your calendar, to-do list, and emails to help you prepare for the day ahead.
  • Daily topic tracking to stay up to date on the latest breakthroughs and trends for any subject you’re following online.
  • Daily market reports tracking your stock portfolio, cryptocurrency prices, and the latest financial news from the past day.
  • Daily weather forecasts paired with outfit ideas based on a list of your personal wardrobe items.
  • Daily practice quizzes to help you master a new language, professional skill, or hobby.
  • Daily creative prompts or artistic inspiration to jumpstart your personal projects every morning.
  • Weekly news digests or details about upcoming tour dates and releases for your favorite musical artists.
  • Weekly rollups of new local cafes and restaurants to check out over the weekend.

Scheduled action notifications

When each response is ready, Gemini will notify you:

  • In the Gemini web app: In the menu under “Chats,” the chat with your scheduled action is marked as unread.
  • In the Gemini mobile app: You’ll get a notification on your mobile device. The notification may appear when your device is locked depending on your settings.
    • Tip: You can turn notifications for Gemini Apps on or off in your device’s app notification settings.

Pause or resume a scheduled action

You can pause an action without deleting the scheduled action. If you pause an action, Gemini won’t run your prompt until you resume the action.

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help Scheduled actions .
  3. Find the scheduled action that you want to pause or resume.
    • To pause an action, turn it off .
    • To resume an action, turn it on .

Edit or delete scheduled action

In the chat with the scheduled action, you can ask Gemini to make changes to the action. These changes will be saved for future occurrences of the action.

You can also edit or delete scheduled actions in your Gemini settings. To do this:

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help Scheduled actions .
  3. Find the scheduled action that you want to edit or delete.
    • To edit the action: Click More Edit. Update the scheduled action, then click Save.
    • To delete the action: Click More Delete.

Scheduled actions & your location

Gemini Apps may use your location to provide more relevant responses to your prompts. For example, to respond to prompts about the weather, Gemini Apps need to know your location.

If you schedule an action that’s related to your location, Gemini Apps will use the location where you created the action for all future responses. To schedule an action for a different location, you can either create a new scheduled action or update your existing action to specify a location.

Learn more about the location information Gemini Apps collect, why, and how it is used.

Why a scheduled action may be turned off

If you aren’t receiving responses for a scheduled action, it may have been automatically turned off due to inactivity. You can turn the scheduled action on again at any time. Learn how to resume a scheduled action.

Upload & analyze files in Gemini Apps

Upload & analyze files in Gemini Apps

You can upload documents, spreadsheets, NotebookLM notebooks, photos, videos, and more to Gemini Apps to get answers, summaries, and insights about your content.

What you need

  • If you’re signed in to a work or school Google Account:
    • To upload files from Google Drive or NotebookLM, access to apps in Gemini must be enabled by your organization’s Workspace administrator. Learn about administrators.
    • Learn more about using Gemini Apps with a work or school account or how to enable access to apps in Gemini Apps.

To use this feature, you must be signed in to Gemini Apps. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

Tip: To get higher limits for this feature, like the ability to upload more files or ask Gemini Apps to reference uploaded files in more chats, you can upgrade to a Google AI plan. Learn more about limits and how to upgrade.

Upload files & code

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. In the text box at the bottom, enter your question or prompt.
  3. Click Add files .
    1. To upload a supported file from your device: click Upload Files .
    2. To add a code folder:click More Uploads Import Code Upload folder.
    3. To add a GitHub repository: More Uploads Import Code and enter the GitHub repository or branch URL. Learn more about adding GitHub repositories.
    4. To add a supported file from your Google Drive: click Add from Drive .
      1. To add files from your Drive, you need to have Keep Activity on and connect Google Workspace to Gemini Apps. If it’s not connected, you’ll get the option to connect it. Learn about your Gemini Apps and Google Workspace data.
    5. To add a NotebookLM notebook: click More Uploads Notebooks .
  4. Click Submit .

Tips:

  • You can add up to 10 (subject to availability) of any kind of supported file in the same prompt, such as documents, images, or videos.
  • If you get an error that Gemini failed to analyze your file correctly, re-upload it.
File types & upload limits
  • Gemini Apps support most file types.
  • Up to 10 files (subject to availability) can be uploaded in the same prompt.
  • Each video can be up to 2 GB. All other supported file types can be up to 100 MB.
  • Total video length can be up to 5 minutes. Upgrade to Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra to extend total upload length to 1 hour.
  • Total audio length can be up to 10 minutes. Upgrade to Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra to extend total upload length to 3 hours.
  • One code folder, or one GitHub repository, with up to 5,000 files and a maximum size of 100 MB, can be added to a chat. Learn more about adding GitHub repositories.
  • ZIP files:
    • Can contain up to 10 files (subject to availability).
    • Can be up to 100 MB.
    • Can’t include video or audio files.

Tip: Based on the data you upload, Gemini can generate visual representations, such as charts, to help illustrate your data.

File upload error messages

“Delete data to upload file”

Gemini Apps have a storage limit for data saved from previous Gemini Apps activity, including your chats and any files you’ve uploaded to Gemini Apps. This limit is independent from your Google Drive or Google Workspace storage limit. If you reach your storage limit in Gemini Apps, you’ll get this error message and you won’t be able to upload files until you clear some storage space.

How to clear storage space in Gemini Apps
If you have a personal Google Account

Important: Chats or Gems with uploaded files such as videos, photos, or files from Google Drive or NotebookLM take up more storage space in Gemini Apps.

To delete your Gemini Apps activity to clear storage space:

  1. Visit gemini.google.com
  2. Click or tap Settings & help Activity .
  3. Choose the Gemini Apps activity your want to delete.

Tip: It may take several minutes for deleted Gemini Apps activity or deleted Gems to clear storage space. If you get the same error message, try waiting before you upload a new file. If you still get the error message, try deleting additional Gemini Apps Activity or Gems.

If you have a Workspace account through work, school, or another organization

Only a Workspace administrator can delete Gemini Apps activity for a work or school account. Learn more about Gemini Apps activity for work and school users.

Contact your administrator to delete Gemini Apps Activity to free up space. Learn how to find your administrator.

“You’ve reached your limit for chats with files”

There are rolling limits for how much you can upload and analyze files in a period of time. After some time, the limit will reset, and you will be able to upload and analyze files again.

If you would like to upload and analyze more files, try again later or upgrade to Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra for higher usage limits.

“Your uploads may be too large for the best results”

If you try to upload a file that is too large, Gemini may provide a response that misses connections or details throughout the content. This is most relevant for prompts that require attention to many details scattered throughout large file(s).

For better results, upload smaller files with less content, or upgrade to Google AI Pro or Google AI Ultra for a larger 1 million token context window.

Important: If you use Deep Think, there is a 192 thousand token window. Learn more about using Deep Think.

What does it mean when my prompt exceeds the context window?

If you’re using Gemini Apps with a work or school Google Account, you might get a message that you’ve exceeded the context window for uploading and analyzing files.

What is a context window?

When you upload files to Gemini Apps, it needs to “read” the content to provide useful insights or answers. The context window is like the reading capacity. It determines how much content can be understood together at one time.

What does it mean when my prompt exceeds the context window?

A larger context window allows Gemini to read and comprehend more. For example, with a 1M token context window, Gemini can understand up to 1,500 pages of text or 30,000 lines of code.

If you exceed the context window, this could lead to responses that don’t take into account all the content provided or miss connections or details throughout the content. This is most relevant for prompts that require attention to many details scattered throughout large files.

Use & manage Connected Apps in Gemini

Use & manage Connected Apps in Gemini

Gemini Apps can connect to other apps to complete your request and give you more helpful responses. With your permission, Gemini can also help you with your info and content in other apps.

Here are a few examples of what you can ask Gemini to help you with:

  • Boost productivity: Summarize emails from Gmail, create events in Google Calendar or third-party apps, or help with code from GitHub.
  • Find & play media: Play music from YouTube Music or Spotify, or search your Google Photos or Samsung Gallery.
  • Connect with people: Make calls and send messages with your default apps or WhatsApp on Android devices.
  • Control your devices: Manage your smart home devices in Google Home or use the Utilities app on Android devices to set alarms, change device settings, and more.

Use Gemini Apps without signing in

On some devices, you can use some Gemini Apps features without signing in your Google Account.

There are some users who can’t use Gemini Apps without signing in. You must sign in to a Google Account to use:

  • The Gemini mobile app on an Android device.

What Gemini Apps features are available when signed out?

When signed out, you can generally use text-based interactions, like asking informational questions or generating simple text. Capabilities may vary and are subject to change.

What Gemini Apps features are not available when signed out?

When signed out, you won’t be able to use features that require Keep Activity to be turned on or advanced capabilities. This includes, but is not limited to:

  • Accessing past chats: Your chat history with Gemini Apps won’t be available.
  • Personalized responses: Gemini Apps won’t be able to tailor responses based on the memory of your past chats or your preferences.
  • Integration with other Google services: Features that rely on Connected Apps (like Google Workspace, Google Photos, or other Google services) won’t be available.
  • Other features that require account authentication: Features like image generation, Gems, and file upload won’t be available.

Why are some features limited when signed out?

Signing in allows us to offer a more tailored and robust experience for users who have agreed to connect Gemini with their Google account, and to our Gemini Apps Privacy Notice.

Tip: If a feature requires sign in, a notification will be included in the Gemini Apps Help Center for that feature.

Verify AI-generated images, videos, and audio

Verify AI-generated images, videos, and audio

You can use the verification tool available within the Gemini App for signed-in users, to help identify images, videos, and audio generated or edited by AI models.

There are two technologies used to check for AI-generated content in Gemini Apps:

  • SynthID:  Uses invisible watermarks to determine if images, videos, and audio were generated or edited specifically by Google’s AI models.
  • Content Credentials: A technology that acts like a digital passport, documenting the digital content’s origin and history, and is used for both AI and non-AI content.

Important: Verification with Content Credentials is available at gemini.google.com and in the Gemini app for Android.  It will be available in the Gemini app for iOS soon.

What you need

To use AI verification, you need:

  • A personal account or qualified Workspace account
  • The latest version of the Gemini App if you use the app to verify content.
  • To be signed in to Gemini Apps.  Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

Upload your content for verification

Important:

  • You can only choose a single image, video, or audio file to verify at a time, and it should have a file size of 100 MB or less.
  • Videos need to be less than 90 seconds each, and audio files need to be less than 1 hour each
  • If you’re taking a screenshot of an image to verify, make sure to crop tight around the image to get maximum accuracy, and don’t upload a collage of multiple distinct images.
  1. On your computer, go to the Gemini web app.
  2. Click Add files .

    • To upload a supported file from your device click Upload Files .

    • To upload a supported file from Google photos, click More Uploads Photos .

    • To add a supported file from your Google Drive, click Add from Drive .

      Tip: To add files from your Drive, you need to have Keep Activity on and connect Google Workspace to Gemini Apps. If it’s not connected, you’ll get the option to connect it. Learn about your Gemini Apps and Google Workspace data.

  3. Ask a verification question such as:
    • “Was this image/video/audio created or edited by Google AI?”
    • “Is this AI-generated?”
    • “Is this a real video?”

About the verification results

Important:

  • While other companies have started to adopt SynthID watermarks, Gemini can currently only recognize content created by Google AI tools.
  • Content Credentials can help provide info about origin and history of content and whether AI tools were used to create or edit it.

After the verification process is complete, Gemini will provide a response based on the results of the verification.

For SynthID
  • If a SynthID watermark is detected, it means all or part of the image or video was created or edited by Google’s AI models.
  • If a SynthID watermark isn’t detected, it means the image or video wasn’t created or edited by Google AI, but it could have been created by other AI systems.
  • In some cases it isn’t clear if the image or video was created or edited by Google AI or not. Some common reasons for this are:
    • “Not enough details to watermark” (e.g., very simple or abstract content).
    • “Likely too small an edit” (minor alterations might not carry a detectable watermark).

For video files, Gemini will state which parts of the video a SynthID watermark was detected. This doesn’t mean it was detected in all parts of that portion of the video.

For Content Credentials

If the content contains Content Credentials, you can view a summary of:

  • Media composition.
  • Edit history.
  • Whether or not AI was used.

Other ways to identify AI-generated content

While content verification in the Gemini app can be a powerful tool, you can also use other methods to identify potentially AI-generated content:

  • Look for visual artifacts: Examine images and videos for inconsistencies or errors that are common in AI-generated content. These can include:
    • Inconsistent or garbled text within the image or video.
    • Errors in small details, such as hands, teeth, or background elements.
    • Inconsistent shadows and lighting.
    • Repetitive patterns that seem unnatural.
  • Reverse image search: Use reverse image search tools (e.g., Google Images) to find original sources or similar images. This can help you determine if the content has a known origin or if it’s new and not created or altered by AI.
  • Metadata analysis: If you have access to the original file (not a screenshot), you can check for embedded information. For photos this can include EXIF data with camera models, dates, and settings.
  • Traces of editing software: Metadata can sometimes show if professional editing software was used.

Common questions about SynthID

What is SynthID?

SynthID is a tool that embeds digital watermarks directly into content generated by Google’s AI models. Currently, it can be used to verify whether images, videos, or audio files were created or edited by Google AI tools. Learn more about SynthID.

Why did Google create SynthID?

Generative AI technologies are rapidly evolving, and AI-generated content is becoming harder to distinguish from content not created or edited by AI. The ability to identify when content is AI-generated helps increase transparency.

Can SynthID still be used if the original AI-generated file is changed?

Yes.  The digital watermark will usually still exist even if the image, video, or audio is re-scaled, re-colored, compressed or altered in other ways. However, there’s still a chance that after many alterations the watermark won’t be detected.

What is the difference between digital watermarks and metadata added to AI-generated content?

Watermarks are embedded directly into content and used for verification purposes. The digital watermarks are not visible to users. Metadata allows content creators to add additional context with original files to provide more information about the content. Both watermarks and metadata are used to increase transparency around AI-generated content.

Is there a limit to the number of checks per day?

There’s a usage quota of approximately 10 image checks, 10 video checks (up to 5 minutes total), and 10 audio checks (up to 3 hours total) within any 24-hour rolling window. If you reach these limits, the Gemini App will notify you.

Common questions about Content Credentials

What are Content Credentials?

Content Credentials are a technology that provides media history and transparency, including whether AI was involved in the creation of the content. It is an industry standard developed by the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity (C2PA), and is supported by many products from different companies.

How do Content Credentials help me make informed decisions?

What Content Credentials do
  • Provide details about the origin and history of content through a standard that works across devices and apps from different companies.
  • Provide information from the app or device maker about AI or non-AI tools used to create or edit an image, video, or audio file.
What Content Credentials don’t do
  • Tell you if an image, video, or audio file is definitely AI-generated, but you can use the origin and history information with the content itself to make informed decisions.

How does Content Credentials info work in Gemini Apps?

Important: Content Credentials verification is available for image, video, or audio files from devices and apps that support compatible versions of the Content Credentials format.

If available, the Content Credentials will:

  • Show the company that provided and cryptographically signed the information. For example, “Info by Google LLC” shows that Google provided the information.
    • The result may list more than one company.

What do these Content Credential errors mean?

If Gemini Apps attempt to verify Content Credentials but there’s an issue, they may display a message saying that the Credentials are invalid. This could be due to these common errors:

  • Incorrectly modified: Content Credentials are built on history that’s maintained and signed by each editor of the file. If the media history was tampered with or modified without an appropriate update of the C2PA data, an error occurs.
  • Incompatible or unsupported: Gemini Apps supports Content Credentials versions 2.2 and later, from products on the C2PA Conforming Products List. Credentials from products outside that list may not be considered valid or trusted. Additionally, some third-party Content Credentials apps store the metadata remotely, separate from the image, video, or audio file; Gemini Apps don’t support remote metadata.
  • Unrecognized: A file may contain malformed Content Credentials when the app that generated the file experienced a bug. Gemini Apps may detect the Credentials, but can’t interpret them in some cases.

Tip: You can also use the Gemini mobile app on some phones. Learn where the Gemini mobile app is available and how to set up the Gemini mobile app.

What you need

To sign in to Gemini Apps, you need one of the following:

  • A personal Google Account.
    • If you manage a Family Link account, you can turn off access to Gemini Apps for users under 13 (or the applicable age in your country) in Google Family Link settings.
  • A work Google Account with a qualifying Workspace edition. You must also be 18 or over.
  • A school Google Account. The service must be enabled by your institution’s administrator.

Additional availability information

  • Learn about supported languages and countries for the Gemini web app.
  • Learn about supported languages and countries for the Gemini mobile app.
  • Learn more about how to use Gemini Apps on your work or school Google Account.
  • To use gemini.google.com, you need access to a supported browser: Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Opera, or Edgium.

Sign in to the Gemini web app

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the top right, select Sign in.
  3. Sign in to your Google Account.

Sign out of the Gemini web app

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the  left, tap Menu  your Profile picture or initial.
  3. Select Sign out.

Can’t sign in to the Gemini web app

If you can’t sign in to your Google Account in the Gemini web app, select the message you get below to learn more.

Can’t access this service

Currently, you can use a personal Google Account that you manage on your own, or a work or school account for which your administrator has enabled access to Gemini. You must be 13 (or the applicable age in your country) or over to use Gemini with a personal or school Google Account and 18 or over to use Gemini with a work account.

You still can’t access the Gemini web app with a Google Account managed by Family Link. If you’re a Google Workspace administrator, learn how to enable access to the Gemini.

Something went wrong

If you get a “Something went wrong” message while trying to access or sign in to the Gemini web app, your account can’t access the app at the moment. This can be due to a variety of reasons, including location, age, or type of account, among others. You can try again later.

To help keep our products and services safe for everyone, we use signals and data to help verify that accounts have a consistent history of abuse-free activity.

For our AI products and services like Gemini Apps, we work hard to make sure there are real users behind accounts.

Manage your tasks with Gemini Spark, schedules & skills

Create & manage schedules for tasks in Gemini Spark

Create & manage schedules for tasks in Gemini Spark

You can put your workflows on autopilot by adding schedules to your tasks. A schedule acts as the automated trigger for a task, telling Gemini Spark exactly when to step in and execute your instructions. You can set these triggers based on time intervals, like every Monday morning, or based on certain conditions, like when an email arrives in your inbox.

To get started, you can schedule a task conversationally with Gemini in a task thread. Just describe what you want Gemini Spark to do and when to do it. You can also visit the Schedules page to create it yourself.

Important: This article covers schedules for tasks in Spark. Scheduled actions are a separate feature that automates certain actions in Gemini chats.

What you need

To use Gemini Spark, you must:

  • Be 18 or over.
  • Sign in to the Gemini app with a personal Google Account with a Google AI Ultra subscription. Learn how to upgrade.
  • Have Keep Activity on.

Important: For now, Gemini Spark is:

  • Available wherever Gemini Apps are supported, except in the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom.
  • Only available in the Gemini mobile app, the Gemini app on Mac, and the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com.

Types of schedules

Gemini currently supports three types of schedules.

  • Time-based: schedule tasks to run once, hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly.
    • For example: “Every day at 7 AM, look through my emails, calendar, and Drive, and let me know what to prioritize for the day”
  • Gmail monitors: schedule tasks to run when you receive an email that satisfies a Gmail filter.
    • For example: “Whenever I receive an email from my manager with an action item for me, help me address the action item and draft a reply.”
  • Topic monitors: monitor topics across news, finance, sports, local events, and more, and schedule tasks to run in response to specific events.
    • For example: “Whenever a new food popup is announced in my city, email me the details and suggest a time on my calendar to check it out.”

While Gemini has improved at monitoring and responding to events more quickly, monitors are still not ideal for tracking fast-moving data or performing time-critical tasks like “Let me know when tickets go on sale immediately so I can buy it.”

Learn how time-based schedules work with time zones.

Create a schedule

Create a schedule conversationally

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark .
  3. In the text box, describe the task you want to schedule.
    • For example:
      • “Every day at 7 AM, look through my emails, calendar, and Drive, and let me know what to prioritize for the day.”
      • “Whenever I receive an email from my manager with an action item for me, help me address the action item and draft a reply.”
    • To specify an existing skill to use, enter 0, start typing the skill name, and select the skill. If it’s off, you can turn it on. Learn more about skills.
  4. Click Submit .

Create a time–based schedule using a blank template

The option to create a schedule manually is only available for time-based schedules.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark Schedules .
  3. On the Schedules page, click Create manually .
  4. Enter a name for the schedule.
  5. Select when you want the task to run.
  6. Enter the instructions for the task.
    • To specify an existing skill to use, enter 0, start typing the skill name, and select the skill. If it’s off, you can turn it on. Learn more about skills.
  7. When you’re done, at the top, click Create. This saves the schedule to your “Ongoing” list.

Tip: To test your new schedule, hover over the schedule, then click More Run now .

Manage your schedules

Track the status of your schedules and modify settings as your needs change.

Find your schedules & check their statuses

You can find a list of the schedules that belong to a task in the task thread’s work panel.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark Tasks .
  3. Click the thread for the task you want to check or manage.
  4. To show the task thread’s work panel, on the left edge of the thread panel, click Close tasks panel . Here, you can view all the schedules that belong to the task.

You can find all the schedules that exist across all your tasks on the Schedules page.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark Schedules .
  3. Review your schedules organized by the following sections:
    • Ongoing: Schedules currently running or ready to run.
    • Paused: Schedules you have temporarily paused.
    • Completed: Schedules that are done running. Completed schedules can only be deleted.

Edit a schedule

Important: If you want to edit a schedule, you can ask Gemini to make the edit within the related task thread. You can also edit schedules from the Schedules page if you can’t find the related task threads.

Step 1: Go to the Schedules page
  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark Schedules .
Step 2: Choose how you want to edit the schedule

To edit with Gemini:

  1. On the Schedules page, hover over the schedule you want to edit.
  2. Click More Edit with Gemini .
  3. In the thread, tell Gemini the changes you want to make.

To edit the schedule directly:

  1. On the Schedules page, click the schedule you want to edit.
  2. Make your changes to the schedule, like when it should run and its instructions.
  3. When you’re done, at the top, click Save .

Tip: To edit the trigger for a schedule that isn’t time-based, use Edit with Gemini .

Pause or resume a schedule

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark Schedules .
  3. Click the schedule you want to pause or resume to go to its details page.
  4. At the top, click More Pause or Resume .

Delete a schedule

Important: If you delete a Spark task thread, it also deletes all schedules in that thread.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
    • On a Mac, you can also open the Gemini app .
  2. On the sidebar, click Switch to Spark Schedules .
  3. Hover over the schedule you want to delete.
  4. Click More Delete .

Fix a problem

I can’t create or turn on a schedule

There are a few reasons why you might not be able to create or turn on a schedule.

  • Active schedules limit reached: The current limit for how many active schedules you can have in Gemini Spark is 50. To create or resume a schedule after reaching this limit, first pause or delete an existing one.
  • Completed schedule: You cannot edit or resume a schedule after it’s marked as complete. You can only delete it.
  • Missing required fields: If you’re creating a schedule from a template but can’t select “Create,” make sure to fill out all sections: the schedule’s name, when it should run, and instructions for the task.

Why didn’t my schedule run on time or run at all?

Here are some reasons that a schedule might not run:

  • Usage limit reached: Gemini Apps have compute-based usage limits that determine how much you can interact with Gemini tools and features. Schedules will not run if you have reached your limit at the time it was set to run. Other features may also be unavailable when you reach your usage limit. Learn more about limits in Gemini Apps.
  • Concurrent task limit reached: You can have at most 15 tasks running at a given time. A schedule will not run if there are already 15 tasks currently running.
  • Schedule run times vary: Scheduled tasks run times are approximate and may not run at the exact moment a time or event condition is met.
  • Delays during high traffic: When there’s a large increase in activity in Gemini Apps, scheduled tasks might be delayed.

Common questions

What’s the difference between a task, schedule, and skill?

To help you get the most out of Spark tasks, it’s helpful to understand the three building blocks that power its logic: tasks, schedules, and skills. Think of these as the what, when, and how.

A task is your high-level goal. It represents a complete project or objective you want Gemini Spark to manage for you.

  • Example: “Plan and manage my business trip to London.”

A schedule lets you hand over tasks to Gemini Spark so they run automatically in the background. You tell Gemini what to do and when to do it. Tasks can be scheduled to run at a specific date and time or in response to an event.

  • Example: “Every day at 8AM (condition), give me an update on AI news (task)”
  • Example: “When my flight is delayed (condition), notify me and propose an update to my itinerary (task).”

Tip: Schedules in Gemini Spark are different from scheduled actions in Gemini chat. Learn how to schedule actions in Gemini Apps.

A skill is a set of reusable instructions and additional context. It teaches Gemini how to do a specific task and what tools to use. You can specify the skill Gemini Spark should use for a task or a schedule’s action. Spark can also automatically use a skill when it’s relevant to a task.

  • Example: Using a “Travel Booking” skill and a “Gmail Writing” skill simultaneously to rebook a room and send a confirmation.

In summary, you define the task (what you want), set the schedules (when it should happen), and provide the skills (how to do it) to complete the work.

What happens if I cancel or downgrade my Google AI subscription?

If you cancel your Google AI subscription or downgrade to a subscription that doesn’t support access to Gemini Spark, you will lose access to Gemini Spark, tasks, schedules, and skills. Your data is retained but some features are paused or disabled:

  • In-progress Spark tasks will finish, but are not deleted.
  • Schedules will be paused, but not deleted.
  • Skills are turned off, but not deleted.

To regain access and resume these features, you’ll need to upgrade or resubscribe to a Google AI subscription that supports Gemini Spark. Learn how to manage your Google AI subscription.

What happens to my schedules if I turn off Gemini Spark?

If you turn Gemini Spark off, any schedules you have will automatically pause.

How do time-based schedules work if I change time zones?

Gemini Spark runs in the cloud instead of on your phone or computer. This means it keeps working even if your device is turned off.

How schedules work across time zones

  • Fixed time zones: When you create a time-based schedule (like a daily summary) in the Gemini app, it’s locked to the timezone of the location where it was created.
  • Travel: Your schedules will continue to run at the original scheduled time, even if you travel to a different timezone.
  • Updating schedules: If you move to a new location and want your routines to adjust to your new local time, simply ask Gemini to “edit the schedule based on my new timezone.”
