How do I manage my mobile permissions when Gemini is my device assistant?

Gemini mobile app (on Android)

Gemini is hosted by the Google app, even if you download the Gemini app . Gemini and the Google app can use various features and capabilities on your device (such as your camera, microphone, contacts, or location) based on your Google app permissions. To review and manage these permissions:

  1. Touch and hold the Google app [Image: Google Search].
  2. Tap App Info Permissions.
  3. To change a permission setting, tap it, then choose Allow or Don’t allow.
Uploads

How does Google work with my uploaded images?

How images in prompts work

You can include an image with your prompt to ask Gemini questions about it, edit it, or use it to generate other content (such as a video). When you add an image to your prompt, or a screenshot through a screen action, such as “Ask about this screen,” Gemini Apps also use Google Lens technology to understand what’s in the image and to read the text. Google uses this information just like any other prompt, as explained in the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice.

What happens when I share a photo or video from a media gallery connected app with Gemini Apps?

If you share a photo or video from a media gallery connected app (like Google Photos) with Gemini Apps, your photo or video is processed according to the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice. This means, for example, that if you use screen actions or the Gemini upload feature to share a photo or video from a media gallery app with Gemini Apps, and if your Keep Activity setting is on, your photo or video is used to improve Google services with the help of human reviewers. Learn more about the Keep Activity setting.

Connected Apps in Gemini

What happens with my data that Gemini, Connected Apps, and other services exchange?

Gemini can use Connected Apps and other services to give you tailored help, find info for you, and help you get more done. For example, if you connect to Google Workspace or Google Photos, you can use Gemini to look up info in your emails or photos. If you ask for recommendations about flights and hotels, Gemini can use publicly available information from Google Flights and Google Hotels to give you tailored help.

What data is shared

Data shared between Gemini and Connected Apps plus other Google services includes:

  • Info from your Gemini chats
  • Info about your device and preferences (like language)
  • Info about your location
  • Info and content from your Connected Apps (like emails, files, events, photos, and videos)
How your data is used

Gemini uses data from Connected Apps per the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice, including to give you tailored help, find info for you, and help you get more done. If you meet certain eligibility requirements and opt in to personalization with certain Connected Apps, Google also uses data from those Connected Apps to personalize your Gemini experience and do things for you, like when you use Gemini Spark or Gemini in Chrome.

Data that Gemini shares with other Google services is used per the Google Privacy Policy, including for product improvement. When you ask Gemini to do things for you, Gemini shares necessary data with others on your behalf to help complete your tasks. Third-party apps use data from Gemini consistent with their own privacy policies and terms.

How to manage your Connected Apps

You can connect and disconnect apps in your Connected Apps settings. Learn how to control which apps Gemini works with.

Some Connected Apps such as Phone, Messages, WhatsApp, and Utilities are available on your Android mobile device, whether Keep Activity is on or off. At this time, other Connected Apps like Google Workspace are unavailable if you turn off Keep Activity. Turning Keep Activity back on restores Gemini’s access to apps that were previously connected.

Disconnecting apps & deleting data
  • Learn how to disconnect apps in Connected Apps settings.
  • Disconnecting an app or deleting data in a connected app doesn’t delete any data from Gemini Apps Activity.
  • You can manage and delete your Gemini Apps activity anytime.
  • Apps retain data that Gemini shares with them subject to their own policies. Deleting data in Gemini Apps Activity doesn’t delete data that other apps have received from Gemini. Learn more about how Google services retain data they collect.
  • Learn how to delete something from a connected app that Gemini remembers about you. If you delete or update data in a connected app, like an email from Gmail or a photo from Google Photos, your experience in Gemini may not be affected until days later.
Things to know
  • If you ask Gemini Apps to change shared content or control shared devices in other services, those actions may be visible to anyone with access to that shared content or device.
  • Before connecting a custom third-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to add a custom connected app, make sure you trust that third-party and understand the supported actions. Google does not control, monitor, or secure these servers.

How can I allow Gemini to personalize my experience with my data from Connected Apps?

Eligible users with Personal Intelligence can connect some Google apps to Gemini to get new, more personalized experiences previously unavailable in Gemini through Connected Apps. Learn more about personalization with your data from Connected Apps.

How is my data used to make calls & send messages with Connected Apps in Gemini?

What data is collected & processed

When you use Connected Apps in Gemini to help you make calls or send messages, Gemini mobile apps collect and process your:

  • Gemini Apps activity (if available)
  • Device calling and messaging logs
  • Contact info
  • Device info and settings

If you previously used Google Assistant to make calls or send messages, up to 90 days of your saved Google Assistant communications request history (for example, “Send a message to Sasha”) may be imported from your Web & App Activity to your Gemini Apps Activity. Learn more about how Gemini Apps get help from Google services.

How data is used

To make calls or send messages with Connected Apps, Gemini mobile apps use your data to:

  1. Choose the most helpful calling or messaging app to use, and
  2. Help you connect with the right person.

Messages that you create and send with the Gemini app are not end-to-end-encrypted by Google.

How to control & manage your data
  • If you don’t want Gemini mobile apps to use your activity to make calls or send messages, you can delete your activity any time in Gemini Apps Activity.
  • You can disconnect supported calling and messaging apps at any time in Connected Apps settings. Learn how to manage Connected Apps in Gemini.
  • You can use supported calling and messaging apps on your mobile device even with Keep Activity off.
  • Calling and messaging apps are not available on smartwatch when Keep Activity is off.

Important: Google Assistant settings, like Assistant on lock screen settings, do not apply to apps connected to Gemini.

Gemini Spark

How does Gemini Spark use my data with the remote browser and remote computer?

When you use the beta Gemini Spark feature, Gemini may use a remote browser or remote computer to help complete your tasks and execute code. This feature is only available when Keep Activity is on. Learn more about Gemini Spark.

When you use the beta Gemini Spark feature on macOS, Gemini can also interact directly with local files you choose to add to your connected folders. For example, Gemini can edit and organize your local files for you. Learn more about Gemini Spark on macOS.

What data is processed

When you use Spark, Gemini uses info from your tasks, schedules, skills, remote browser, remote computer, and any other available sources, like Connect Apps, Personal Intelligence, and info from websites it interacts with, including those you are logged into.

  • Remote browser: Gemini processes information from your browser session, like cookies that contain your website authentication info, and page content.
  • Remote computer: Gemini saves and executes .md files, code and other information related to your tasks. This saved information can include data you find sensitive from sources like Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps that Spark has used to understand and process your tasks.

This data is used consistently with the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice, including to make it easier for you to use the remote browser and remote computer in future chats. You can delete this data at any time in your Gemini Spark settings.

What data is shared

To complete your tasks, including through your Connected Apps and the remote browser, Gemini will share with other services and third parties necessary info, which can include data like your name and address or info you find sensitive. This info may include data from your Connected Apps and remote computer files.

How to control & manage your data

Remote browser: You can interrupt Gemini Spark’s actions on the remote browser by selecting  Stop in the prompt text box or Take Control in the remote browser.

You can also delete remote browser data in your Gemini Spark settings. This will sign you out of all sites in the remote browser.

Remote computer: You can manage or clear your code execution history and files directly within your Gemini Spark settings.

What happens when you turn off Gemini Spark?

If you turn Gemini Spark off:

  • Your remote browser data and remote computer data is deleted
  • Your schedules and tasks are paused and not deleted
  • Your chats are not deleted but you can manage them anytime in Gemini Apps Activity
  • Gemini Spark on macOS will no longer have access to local files in your connected folders

If you turn Gemini Spark back on:

  • Gemini will automatically resume paused tasks and schedules

What happens with my data when Gemini uses screen automation to help me get tasks done in Android apps?

Creating an avatar involves recording your voice and face. Google uses that data to generate AI content using your avatar across certain Google services, including Gemini Apps, and to protect Google, our users, and the public.

Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy

Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy

How Google enforces the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy

Generative AI models can help you explore, learn, and create. We expect you to engage with them in a responsible, legal, and safe manner. However, some restrictions apply to your interactions with generative AI in Google products and services. These restrictions are set out in the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.

Learn more about these restrictions and our specific Terms of Service.

How Google identifies potential violations of the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy

We use a combination of automated systems and human review to detect activity and behavior that suggest misuse of our GenAI products, for example:

  • Attempting to generate content to engage in dangerous or illegal activities, or otherwise violate applicable law or regulations.
  • Compromising the security of Google’s services, including attempts to circumvent safety protections (e.g. prompt injections).
  • Attempting to generate content that violates privacy, including using someone’s image without their consent and non-consensual intimate imagery.
  • Using generated content to engage in frauds, scams or other deceptive actions.
  • Attempting to generate of content related to child sexual abuse or exploitation.
When Prohibited Use Policy violations are confirmed

If we confirm that you have violated the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy or our other specific Terms of Service, you will receive notifications in-product and/or via email. Repeated violations of the Prohibited Use Policy may lead to restrictions to your Generative AI product usage and/or your Google account.

Appeal Process

If your account was restricted for violating the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy, and you feel this may have been in error, you can appeal the restriction by submitting an appeal using the link from the restriction notice or email.

How Gemini Apps help protect users from malicious content & prompt injection

How Gemini Apps help protect users from malicious content & prompt injection

Learn how Gemini Apps help protect users from malicious content and prompt injection attacks.

Malicious content & prompt injection in generative AI

Similar to email and content threats like malware and phishing attacks, security threats can target generative AI tools. Prompt injection is an attempt to elicit an unintended or harmful response from generative AI tools. Attackers may commit prompt injection not only by directly submitting queries, but also by sharing malicious content with a user, who then unintentionally references this malicious content in prompts in generative AI tools like Gemini Apps or Gemini for Workspace.

To help protect Gemini users, Google uses advanced security measures to identify risky and suspicious content.

How Google helps detect malicious content & prompt injection

To help protect you from malicious content and prompt injection, Gemini Apps may block some inputs if suspicious activity is detected.

When Gemini identifies activity related to a prompt that may be suspicious
  • Gemini Apps provides a warning notification that the content has security risks
  • Sometimes none of the content can be used to generate a response
  • Sometimes only some of the content is used to generate a response, with the suspicious content excluded by Gemini

For example, if you ask Gemini Apps to summarize email messages, and one of those messages has malicious content, Gemini may not respond to your prompt for safety reasons.

Help avoid unsafe content

Pay attention when interacting with content from someone you don’t know
  • Take notice of warnings from Google on content you receive in other tools like Gmail
  • Avoid clicking links from untrustworthy sources
  • Use caution when interacting with shared content, like public Gemini Apps chats or Gemini Canvas web apps, from unknown providers
Malicious content and prompt injections in generative AI

If you get a response that’s inaccurate or that you feel is unsafe, you can give feedback on that response to let us know.

Learn how to report a problem with Gemini Apps.

Manage & delete your activity in Gemini Apps

Manage & delete your activity in Gemini Apps

When you are signed in and Keep Activity is on, Google stores your Gemini Apps activity in your Google Account. You can review your prompts, delete your Gemini Apps activity, and turn off Keep Activity in My Activity at any time.

For more info about your Gemini Apps data and how you can manage it, go to the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub.

Important:

  • To manage Gemini Apps Activity, you need to sign in to Gemini Apps. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • This article covers Gemini Apps activity for a personal account. If you use Gemini Apps with a work or school account, your Gemini Apps Activity settings are controlled by your Google Workspace administrator. You may not be able to change your retention settings or see how long your chats are retained for Learn more about Gemini Apps activity for work and school users.

Find your Gemini Apps activity

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Click Settings & help Activity .
    • You can also go to myactivity.google.com/product/gemini.

Go to Gemini Apps Activity

Tips to find specific Gemini Apps activity
  • For conversations with Gems, the Gem used is noted in your Gemini Apps activity.
  • For Gemini Live chats, the transcripts, audio, files, images, & YouTube videos, and any video or screenshares you choose to share with Live are saved in Gemini Apps Activity if your Keep Activity setting is on.
  • If activity includes specific data from your Live chat, it shows a related icon below it.
    • An audio icon means it includes audio.
    • A screen sharing icon means it includes video frames of your shared screen.
    • A video icon means it includes video frames of your camera stream.
    • To view or download this audio, screenshare, or video data, select Details.

Delete your activity

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Click Settings & help Activity .
    • You can also go to myactivity.google.com/product/gemini.
  3. Choose the Gemini Apps activity you want to delete. You can choose:
    • All your Gemini Apps activity: Above your activity, click Delete All time.
    • The last hour or day: Above your activity, click Delete Last hour or Last day.
    • A specific time period: Above your activity, click Delete Custom range.
    • A specific day: Next to the day, click Delete all activity from [day] .
    • A specific activity: Next to the activity, click Delete activity item .
What happens when Gemini Apps activity is deleted
  • If a conversation with a Gem is deleted, it doesn’t delete the Gem. Learn how to delete your Gems.
  • If a shared chat is deleted, it doesn’t delete the related public link. Learn how to delete a public link.
  • If you delete activity for a Gemini Live chat, any related audio, transcript, videos, and screenshares for that activity are also deleted.

Turn off Keep Activity

Important:

  • If you’re 18 or over, Keep Activity is on by default.
  • If Keep Activity is off, any Gems you create will still be saved to your account. Any chats you create with Gems will not be saved. Learn more about what happens with your data when you use Gems.

To turn off Keep Activity:

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Click Settings & help Activity .
  3. Near the top, click On Turn off or Turn off and delete activity.
    • Even when Keep Activity is off, your conversations will be saved with your account for up to 72 hours to allow Google to provide the service and process any feedback. This activity won’t appear in your Gemini Apps Activity.

When Keep Activity is off

If Keep Activity is turned off, only the following apps are available:

  • Utilities
  • Phone
  • Messages
  • WhatsApp

Learn how to turn off the Utilities, Phone, Messages or WhatsApp apps.

The following connected apps and integrated services will not be available when this setting is off:

  • Workspace (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Docs, Google Drive, Google Keep, and Google tasks)
  • Google Home
  • Google Flights
  • Google Hotels
  • Google Maps
  • Google Photos
  • Spotify
  • YouTube
  • YouTube Music
  • OpenStax

Learn how to turn Keep Activity on or off.

Manage whether your audio & Gemini Live recordings are used to improve Google services

Important:

  • This setting is off by default.
  • To turn on this setting, you must have Keep Activity on.

You can let Google use your audio and Gemini Live videos and screenshares to improve and develop its services, including training generative AI models. Learn more about this setting.

To turn on this setting:

  1. Click Settings & help Activity .
    • If Keep Activity is off, click Off. Then review the disclosures and click Turn on.
  2. Next to Improve Google services with your audio and Gemini Live videos & screenshares, select the box.
  3. Click Turn on.

Tip: You can turn off this setting at any time.

Change Auto-delete settings

By default, your Gemini Apps activity older than 18 months is auto-deleted. You can turn off Auto-delete or change the auto-delete period to 3 or 36 months.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Click Settings & help Activity .
  3. Near the top, click Deleting activity older than … months or Choose an auto-delete option.
  4. Choose how long your Gemini Apps activity is kept (3, 18, or 36 months) or select Don’t auto-delete activity.
  5. Click Next and follow the on-screen instructions.

How your Gemini Apps activity is deleted from your Google Account

When you choose to delete activity manually or activity is deleted automatically, we immediately start the process of removing it from the product and our systems.

First, we aim to immediately remove it from view. Then, we begin a process designed to safely and completely delete the data from our storage systems.

Learn more about how Google helps you delete data from your account.

Report Google AI policy violations that involve your likeness

Report Google AI policy violations that involve your likeness

You can report instances where you believe your likeness has been generated or altered by someone else with Google’s generative AI tools without your consent. This process helps Google address violations of its policies and maintain a safe and respectful environment for all users.

Important: Currently, complaints are supported for images and videos.

What you need

To submit a complaint, you must be:

  • Signed in with a personal Google Account. Work or school accounts are not supported for this process.
  • At least 18 years old.
  • Located in a region where Google’s selfie verification service is available.

What you can report

This process is specifically designed for reporting situations where:

  • Your likeness has been generated or altered by another user through Google’s generative AI tools, specifically image or video creation with Gemini Apps.
    • You can report videos even if only part of the video is AI generated.
  • This generation or modification occurred without your explicit consent.

Such actions may violate Google’s Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.

What you can’t report

This complaint process can’t be used:

  • To make a content removal request. If you believe content is illegal and requires removal, please use Google’s general content reporting tools at reportcontent.google.com.
  • To report non AI-generated intimate or sexual content that was distributed without your consent. To help prevent non-consensual sharing of the intimate images across both Google and other platforms, create a case with StopNCII.
    • Learn more about how to submit a request for removal of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII).
  • To report content generated by third-party AI models or tools that are not developed or offered by Google. For this content, find the policy of the AI platform that was used to create or modify your likeness.
  • To upload an audio file as part of a complaint. These aren’t supported at this time.
  • To report non-AI-generated clips that are included within a merged video.

Submit a likeness complaint

  1. Go to the Google AI Likeness Abuse complaint form.
  2. Sign in with your personal Google Account.
  3. You will be redirected to complete a selfie verification and liveness check, which are necessary to validate your complaint.
  4. Fill out the complaint form with the required and optional information:
    • Full Name (Required): Enter your full legal name.
    • Country of residence (Required): Select your country from the dropdown menu.
    • AI-generated content (Required): Upload one image or video that contains the generation or modification of your likeness.
      • Supported file types:
        • Images: 0 with a maximum file size of 50MB
        • Videos: 0, with a duration between 4 and 60 seconds with a maximum file size of 100MB.
          • For videos containing multiple clips, a single complaint should be filed for the entire video. Upload the video in its most original format downloaded from the source.
      • If our automated system determines that Google AI did not create the content you upload, the submission process won’t proceed and you won’t be able to submit the form.
    • URL of Content (Optional): Provide one URL to the specific content (e.g., webpage, image link, or video link) where your likeness was displayed. This information can help Google process your request more efficiently.
    • Screenshot (Optional): Upload one screenshot that provides additional context regarding the abusive content. (For instance, you might include a screenshot of a group chat that provides more context on the AI-generated content)
      • Supported file types: .0
      • Maximum file size: 25MB
  5. Follow the onscreen instructions to complete the selfie verification. This will help us verify that you are the person shown in the AI-generated content.

What happens after you submit

  • Upon successful submission, you will receive a confirmation message such as “We got your complaint and are reviewing it.” At this time, we cannot provide you with further updates on the status of our investigation.
  • If your complaint is substantiated, Google may take appropriate action, which could include blocking or restricting the account of the user who generated your likeness.

Set up & control personalization in Gemini Apps

About personalization with Connected Apps

About personalization with Connected Apps

Eligible users with Personal Intelligence can connect their data in some Google apps to Gemini to get new, more personalized experiences previously unavailable in Gemini through Connected Apps. Learn more about eligibility.

If you connect certain apps to Gemini, your data from those apps and from your Google Account is used to:

  • personalize your Gemini experience with insights about you, your relationships, and people in your world
  • do things for you, like make recommendations based on your preferences, or create a tailored itinerary
  • improve Google services, including training generative AI models, for everyone

Apps you can connect

You can connect your data in these apps to Gemini:

  • Google Photos (if eligible)
  • YouTube
  • Google Workspace, which includes services like Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Keep, Tasks, Chat, and Meet
  • Google Search services, which include Search (including AI Mode and Discover), Maps, Shopping, Flights, Hotels, Translate, and News
  • Contacts, which includes Google Contacts and contact info from your signed-in device (US only, English only, and requires an AI Ultra subscription)

What data is used

Data shared between Gemini and Connected Apps includes things like your saved data from Search services and YouTube, emails, files, events, photos, videos, info about your contacts (such as phone numbers, addresses, and birthdays), and location info (from your IP address, device, and content), as well as insights drawn from them. Data shared may relate to topics you find sensitive, like race, religion, and health, or confidential info.

How your data is used

This data is used to create personal insights about you, your relationships, and the people and things in your world. For example, depending on your settings, your Google Photos data is used to infer your interests, relationships to people in your photos, and where you’ve been, including by associating your face with corresponding location data and timestamps. This data is also used to do things for you, like look up your info or add items to your grocery list, and to improve Google services, including training generative AI.

Data from Connected Apps is used and human reviewed per the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice.

Learn more about what data from Google Workspace and Google Photos is used, including for training and human review, and steps we take to protect your privacy.

Gemini shares data from Connected Apps with other services as needed to interact with you (like when Gemini uses Maps to give you directions). Data Gemini shares with other Google services is used per the Google Privacy Policy, including for product improvement. If you use Gemini to interact with third-party services, they process your data according to their own privacy policies.

What’s not changing

Your choices here don’t change other personalization settings. For example, if your Memory setting is on, Gemini still uses your past chats to personalize your experience. Your choices here also don’t change whether other services exchange data and whether Connected Apps use data to improve their own services. Other services continue personalizing and exchanging data based on their own settings.

Your choices here also don’t change whether contacts are saved or used by Google services, including Gemini, based on other settings. For example, if the “Save contact info from your devices” setting is on, information about your contacts from your signed-in devices will be used by Gemini to make these contacts easier to interact with across Google services.

Your choices here also don’t change Gemini’s use of public data. For example, if Search services and YouTube aren’t connected, Gemini can still use public websites and videos in Google Search and YouTube to respond to you.

Disconnecting apps and deleting your data

Disconnecting an app or deleting data in a connected app doesn’t delete any data from Gemini Apps Activity. You can manage and delete your Gemini Apps activity anytime. Deleting Gemini Apps activity also doesn’t delete data in other services. If you delete or update data in a connected app, your experience in Gemini may not be affected until days later. Learn more about how these services retain data they collect.

Enhance your Personal Intelligence

To unlock your personalization experience, you may need to turn on other settings, like Face Groups in Photos and your Workspace smart feature setting.

You’re in control

You can manage which apps are connected in Personal Intelligence. You can also manage and delete your Gemini Apps activity anytime and control whether your future Gemini Apps activity is used to improve Google AI.

Common questions

Do you train AI models on my personal data? If so, what data do you train on, and do you train on my entire Gmail inbox or Google Photos library?

How your Connected Apps data is used to improve Google services

Gemini Apps activity, which includes data from apps you connect, is used to improve Google services for everyone, including by training generative AI models, if your Keep Activity setting is on.

Below are more details on things we do and don’t do.

Gemini does not train generative AI models directly on your Gmail inbox, Drive, Contacts, Calendar or other Workspace apps or on imagery or audio from your Google Photos library. When you interact with Gemini, summaries, excerpts, generated media, and inferences from your relevant media, emails, and files may be used to help us answer your prompts. To make our responses relevant, helpful, and high quality, we train our generative AI models off of these summaries, excerpts, generated media, and inferences. In some cases, for example, where the email or file is brief or particularly relevant to respond to the prompt, the summary may just be the email or file.

We also train generative AI models on data like:

  • Your prompts in Gemini Apps,
  • The responses and suggestions that Gemini Apps give you, and
  • Information about how our models generated those responses and suggestions.

For example, if you ask Gemini, “Plan a list of restaurants for my upcoming trip,” our models might review your emails to get information about your upcoming hotel reservation and flight itinerary, as well as restaurants you’ve visited on prior trips. Gemini would then summarize that information to give you personalized restaurant recommendations close to your hotel at your destination.

How we protect your privacy

We take steps to reduce personal information from interactions personalized using Connected Apps or apply privacy preserving techniques like differential privacy before using them to train generative AI models powering our services, unless it’s to address abuse or harm.

Important: Please don’t connect apps to Gemini if they contain personal or confidential information that you wouldn’t want to be used for training generative AI models.

Tip: Even if you choose not to connect an app, you can still use Gemini screen actions and the Gemini upload feature. If you choose to use these features and your Keep Activity setting is on, your screenshots and uploads of things like your media and files could be used to improve Google services with the help of human reviewers.

What can I do if I don’t want you to use my data to train your AI models?

You can manage which apps are connected in Personal Intelligence and still use Gemini Apps even if you choose not to connect any apps to them. You can also manage and delete your Gemini Apps activity anytime and turn off Keep Activity to stop your future chats from being used to improve Google AI.

If you disconnect a connected app or delete any data in that app, it doesn’t delete any data from Gemini Apps Activity. That data can still be used for product improvement, including training generative AI models. You can delete your Gemini Apps activity to prevent it from being used for future product improvement, unless it has already been reviewed by trained reviewers. Learn how to manage & delete your Gemini Apps activity.

Based on your other Google Account and product settings, Google services may collect data, share data, or personalize your experience. To check your Google Account settings, go to account.google.com.

Will human reviewers have access to my data?

How human review helps improve Google services

When connected to Gemini, a subset of Connected Apps data processed by Gemini is reviewed by human reviewers (including trained service providers) to debug our services, help keep them safe, and improve them.

Human reviewers improve Google services, including generative AI. Reviewers assess if Gemini responses were low-quality, inaccurate, or harmful. They also suggest better responses. We use their suggestions to help our models respond better in the future.

Important: Please don’t connect your apps to Gemini Apps if they contain confidential information that you wouldn’t want a reviewer to see.

What data is included in human review

The subset of Connected Apps data that’s reviewed by the human reviewers includes:

  • Interactions, summaries, excerpts and inferences from your relevant emails and files.
    • In some cases, for example, where the email or file is brief or particularly relevant to respond to the prompt, the summary may just be the email or file.
  • Summaries, inferences, and generated media based on your Google Photos library, if you’re eligible to connect Google Photos to Gemini Apps.
    • Except for cases of abuse and harm or when you submit feedback, humans don’t view media from your Google Photos library.
  • Data like your prompts in Gemini Apps, responses and suggestions that Gemini Apps give you, and information about how our models generated those responses and suggestions.
How we protect your privacy in this process

Before trained service providers review interactions personalized using Connected Apps, we take steps to protect your privacy, such as disconnecting interactions from your Google Account and reducing personal information in this data, unless it’s to address abuse or harm. If you submitted feedback, or we need to address abuse or harm, human reviewers may also review some of your Gmail inbox or Photos library media.

Connect your Google apps to personalize your Gemini experience

Connect your Google apps to personalize your Gemini experience

You can get personalized Gemini experiences that are uniquely helpful to you using Personal Intelligence. When you connect Google apps that work with Personal Intelligence, Gemini can:

  • Personalize your experience with insights about you, your relationships, and people in your world.

  • Do things for you, like make recommendations based on your preferences, or create a tailored itinerary.

  • Find and summarize information from these apps. For example, you can ask “What did I search for last month?”

  • Get content from Gmail and Google Photos, like photos from your last vacation.

  • Create and edit personalized images based on your unique style, life, and preferences. Learn more about how to generate and edit images.

You can control which apps are connected at any time from your Connected Apps settings.

Important: Personal Intelligence is being released gradually and may not be available to you just yet.

What you need

To get Gemini with Personal Intelligence, you need to:

  • Be 18 or over.
  • Sign in with a personal Google Account. This feature isn’t available when you sign in to a work, school, or supervised Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have Keep Activity on. This feature isn’t available when this setting is off.

Additional requirements

To get personalized Gemini experiences based on your data in other Google apps:

  • Have Web & App Activity on. Personalization in Gemini based on your Search services data isn’t available when this setting is off. Learn how to manage your Web & App Activity.
  • Have YouTube History on. Personalization in Gemini based on your YouTube activity isn’t available when this setting is off. Learn how to manage your YouTube watch history and YouTube search history.
  • Have Smart features in other Google products on. Gemini Apps can’t connect to Google Workspace when this setting is off. Learn how to change smart features settings.
  • Meet eligibility criteria for Google Photos. Connecting Google Photos to Gemini Apps is only available in certain countries and territories. Before Gemini Apps can personalize your experience based on your Photos data, you’ll need to complete the following steps in Google Photos:
    • Turn on Face Groups and select which face is yours. Learn how to turn on Face Groups and how to select your face group.
    • Turn on Estimate missing locations if not enabled. Learn how to turn on Estimate missing locations.

Important: For now, this feature is:

  • Not available in the European Economic Area, Nigeria, Switzerland, or the United Kingdom.
  • Only available in the Gemini mobile app, the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com, Gemini in Chrome (in countries where Gemini in Chrome is available), and Gemini on your smartwatch.
  • Not available in certain features, like Gems.

Connect your Google apps

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. If you’re eligible, a card will show where you can opt in to Personal Intelligence in Gemini.
  3. Click Get started.
  4. Choose which apps to connect to Gemini.
    • To connect all available apps, click Connect all.
    • To choose which apps to connect, click Choose apps.
    • Or click Don’t connect.
  5. Follow any on-screen instructions.

Manage in Connected Apps settings

What Google apps work with Personal Intelligence

For now, only the following Google apps work with Personal Intelligence in Gemini:

  • Contacts, which includes contacts data from Google Contacts and your device, and insights derived from them.
  • Google Photos (in certain countries and territories), which includes your photos and videos, and insights derived from these.
  • Google Workspace, which includes your content in services like Gmail, Calendar, and Drive. Learn more about the services included.
  • Search services, which includes your saved data in services like Search, Maps, and Shopping. Learn more about the services included.
  • YouTube, which includes your YouTube History.

Turn off Personal Intelligence for a chat

Important: We’re gradually releasing this feature, so it might not be available to you just yet.

If you don’t want a specific Gemini chat to be personalized using Personal Intelligence, you can turn it off. When it’s off, your chat won’t be personalized based on the memory of your Gemini chats, instructions for Gemini, or info from Connected Apps.

  1. In the text box, click Tools .
  2. Turn Personal Intelligence off.
    • If you turn off Personal Intelligence during your chat, Gemini can still use earlier parts of that chat as context.
    • Gemini remembers your setting choice for this chat. It’ll be the same if you leave the chat and continue it later.
    • If you start a new chat, Personal Intelligence is on by default.

Tips:

  • To regenerate a personalized response without personalization, you can also select Try without personalization.
  • If you turn off Personal Intelligence, it doesn’t stop your chat from being saved to Gemini Apps Activity and used to personalize a response in another chat. To chat without saving activity to your Google Account, use a temporary chat. Learn how to start a temporary chat.

Manage your Connected Apps

Important:

  • Only certain Google apps work with Personal Intelligence in Gemini.
  • Learn more about what happens when you disconnect an app in Gemini.

You can change the apps that personalize your Gemini Apps experiences in your Connected Apps settings at any time.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help Personal Intelligence Connected Apps.
  3. Disconnect or connect Contacts, Google Photos (if available), Google Workspace, Search services, or YouTube.
    • To disconnect an app, turn it off .
    • To connect an app, turn it on .
  4. Follow any on-screen instructions.

Tip: Gemini Apps can still use public information from certain Google services, like Google Search and YouTube, even if the app is disconnected for Personal Intelligence. Learn more about the Google services Gemini uses public info from.

Delete something Gemini knows about you from a connected app

If you want to delete something that Gemini remembered about you:

  1. Delete all chats with this info from Gemini Apps Activity or Recent chats. Learn how to manage your Gemini Apps Activity and delete a chat from Recent chats.
  2. Disconnect the app with this info, so Gemini doesn’t use it again. Learn how to manage your Connected Apps.

You must complete both steps because:

  • If you only disconnect the app, Gemini might still use the info if it’s in a past chat.
  • If you only delete the chats, Gemini might still find the info in the connected app.
What happens when you delete data from a connected app

If you delete or update data in a connected app, like an email from Gmail or photo from Google Photos, your experience in Gemini may not be affected until days later.

How Personal Intelligence improves your Connected Apps experience

Before, Gemini was great at finding info from your apps. With Personal Intelligence:

  • Gemini has access to your data from more Connected Apps like Contacts, Google Workspace, Google Photos (if available), Search services, and YouTube.
  • Gemini can connect and understand your info across Connected Apps.

This allows Gemini to:

  • Handle complex, multi-step requests across those apps.
  • Understand the context and how your info across those apps are related.
  • Provide more personalized responses based on your info from Connected Apps.

Fix a problem

I’ve previously connected the Google Workspace and Google Photos apps. Why are they now disconnected?

If you’ve previously connected the Google Workspace app or the Google Photos app, your settings have been reset with the launch of Personal Intelligence with Connected Apps. If you want, you can reconnect those apps with Personal Intelligence.

Gemini’s info about me is wrong. How can I correct it?

To correct what Gemini knows about you and uses in a response:

  1. Make sure that Memory is turned on. Learn how to turn Memory on or off.
  2. Correct Gemini directly in your chat.

While Gemini continues to improve, it might not always get it right.

Why is my experience different across Gemini Apps?

If you’re eligible for Personal Intelligence in Gemini but your personalized experience is different across Gemini Apps, make sure you’re signed in to the same personal Google Account across your Gemini Apps. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

I’m eligible for Personal Intelligence in Gemini but don’t get the option to opt in.

Important: Personal Intelligence is being released gradually and may not be available to you just yet.

If you meet the eligibility criteria but don’t get the option to opt in to Personal Intelligence, try connecting the Google Workspace and Google Photos apps (if available) in Connected Apps settings. You may have additional steps to set up and connect those apps.

  • Connect the Google Workspace app and confirm Smart features in other Google products is on.
  • Connect the Google Photos app and complete the setup steps, which includes turning on Face Groups and selecting which face is yours if you haven’t done so already.

If you don’t want to get personalization based on your content and info in these apps, you can disconnect them at any time in your Connected Apps settings.

How your data is handled

Learn more about how your data is handled when Gemini works with Connected Apps.

Get personalization in Gemini Apps

You can get a personalized experience in Gemini Apps based on:

  • The memory of your past Gemini chats
  • Your content and activity in certain Google apps you connect to Gemini
  • Your preferences, like instructions on how you want Gemini to respond

Important:

  • These features are not available to everyone at this time. You can find details about each feature in the articles linked below.
  • To use these features, you must sign in to Gemini Apps with a personal Google Account. These features are not available while signed in to a work, school, or supervised account.

Get personalization with memory of your past Gemini chats

Get personalization with memory of your past Gemini chats

You can get a personalized experience from Gemini Apps using memory of your past chats. With this feature, Gemini can learn from your chats to understand more about you and your world.

What you need

To get personalization with memory of your past Gemini chats, you need to:

  • Be 18 or over.
  • Sign in with a personal Google Account. This feature isn’t available when you sign in to a work, school, or supervised Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have Keep Activity on. This feature isn’t available when this setting is off.

Important: For now, this feature is:

  • Only available in the Gemini mobile app, the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com, Gemini in Chrome (in countries where Gemini in Chrome is available), and Gemini on your smartwatch.
  • Not available in certain features, like Gems or Live chats. In a text chat, you can ask Gemini to reference a past Gemini Live conversation.

Turn Memory on or off

You can change whether Gemini Apps use memory of your past chats to personalize your experience at any time.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help Personal Intelligence.
  3. Turn Memory off or on .

Find & delete your past Gemini chats

You can find and delete your past chats in Gemini Apps Activity. If you delete a chat, there might be a short delay before Gemini stops using it to personalize your responses. Learn how to manage your Gemini Apps activity.

Check if Gemini used your past chats

To check if Gemini used your past chats, just ask Gemini, “Did you use any info from past chats?”

Delete or correct something Gemini knows about you

To delete something that Gemini remembered about you, delete all chats with this info from Gemini Apps Activity. Learn how to manage your Gemini Apps.

To correct what Gemini knows about you and uses in a response:

  1. Make sure that Memory is turned on. Learn how to turn Memory on or off.
  2. Correct Gemini directly in your chat.

While Gemini continues to improve, it might not always get it right.

Delete something Gemini knows about you from a connected app

If you want to delete something that Gemini remembered about you:

  1. Delete all chats with this info from Gemini Apps Activity or Recent chats. Learn how to manage your Gemini Apps Activity and delete a chat from Recent chats.
  2. Disconnect the app with this info, so Gemini doesn’t use it again. Learn how to manage your Connected Apps.

You must complete both steps because:

  • If you only disconnect the app, Gemini might still use the info if it’s in a past chat.
  • If you only delete the chats, Gemini might still find the info in the connected app.
What happens when you delete data from a connected app

If you delete or update data in a connected app, like an email from Gmail or photo from Google Photos, your experience in Gemini may not be affected until days later.

Get started with your daily brief in Gemini Apps

Get started with your daily brief in Gemini Apps

You can get proactive, personalized updates in your daily brief in Gemini Apps. Gemini generates items in your daily brief so you can stay informed, take timely action, and progress toward your goals. It summarizes important information from your Connected Apps, like Gmail and Google Calendar, and your Gemini chats to help you manage your daily life and plan ahead.

  • For students: Manage class schedules, organize study plans, and track applications.
  • For entrepreneurs: Surface actionable client emails and update task reminders.
  • For parents: Manage school communications, track family milestones, and handle household tasks.
  • For job seekers: Quickly act on recruiter inquiries, prepare for interviews, and monitor application statuses.

What you need

To get a daily brief, you must:

  • Be 18 or over and in the US.
  • Sign in to Gemini Apps with a personal Google Account. This feature is not available with a work, school, or supervised Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have a Google AI subscription. This feature is only available with a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription on your personal account.
  • Be eligible for Personal Intelligence and do the following:
    • Connect Google Workspace to Gemini Apps. Learn how to connect Google apps with Personal Intelligence.
    • Turn on Memory. Learn how to turn on Memory.

Important: For now, a daily brief is:

  • Only available in English.
  • Only available in the Gemini mobile app and the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com.

Find your daily brief

If you’re eligible for a daily brief, you can access your daily brief from the sidebar.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. On the sidebar, click Daily brief .

About your daily brief

Your daily brief includes two main sections that help you manage your tasks and goals.

  • Top of mind: This section shows timely, actionable items. These items primarily come from your Gmail, Calendar, and Gemini chats. This helps you stay informed about your most important updates each day.
  • Looking ahead: This section focuses on your longer-term goals. It provides suggested next steps to help you achieve them. Gemini’s AI models generate these suggestions using insights from your Personal Intelligence.

Review & manage items in your daily brief

You can chat about items in your daily brief, mark them complete, and give feedback on them. This helps Gemini understand what’s important to you and better personalize your future updates.

Chat about an item

Important: If you start a chat about an item, the chat is saved to Gemini Apps Activity. Learn how to manage your Gemini Apps activity.

You can chat with Gemini about a specific item from your daily brief. This helps improve Gemini’s understanding and personalizes future content.

  1. In your daily brief, find the item you want to chat about.
  2. Below the item, click More Chat .
  3. In the text box, enter your question or feedback.

Mark an item complete or dismiss it

You can mark an item as complete after you’ve addressed it or dismiss it. This helps Gemini understand your progress and adjust future recommendations.

  1. In your daily brief, find the item you want to mark complete.
  2. Below the item, click More Mark complete or Dismiss .

To change an item back to incomplete: In your daily brief, click the completed item Mark incomplete [Image: Mark incomplete].

Check an item’s source

  1. Below an item in your daily brief, click More .
  2. You can find the item’s source in the popup window.

Give feedback on an item

You can tell Gemini whether an item is helpful or not. This guides Gemini in personalizing your daily brief.

  1. In your daily brief, find the item you want to give feedback on.
  2. Below the item, click More Helpful or Not helpful .

Turn off Daily brief

Daily brief is designed to work automatically if you’re eligible. You can turn it off at any time.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help Personal Intelligence.
  3. Turn off Daily brief.

Ask about your Google Classroom assignments, classes & more in Gemini Apps

Ask about your Google Classroom assignments, classes & more in Gemini Apps

You can get quick answers, stay organized, and plan ahead for your classes with Google Classroom in Gemini Apps. For example, you can:

  • As an educator: Manage your course material, review student work and progress, get information on upcoming tasks, draft assignments and announcements, and more.
  • As a student: Quickly find course information, check assignment details and due dates, and get summaries about coursework.

Important:

  • If you’re signed in to a school account, the ability to connect Google Classroom app with Gemini is enabled by default unless your admin disabled it. If enabled, you can disconnect the Google Classroom app anytime in your Connected Apps settings.
  • When you use the Google Classroom app in Gemini, your data is protected by enterprise-grade security and privacy. Learn more in the Generative AI in Google Workspace Privacy Hub.

What you need

To connect Google Classroom to Gemini Apps, you need to:

  • Be designated as 18 or over by your administrator. Learn more about Gemini feature access by age.
  • Be signed in to the Gemini app with a work or school account. This feature isn’t available if you sign in to a personal Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have your admin enable the Google Classroom app in Gemini. Only your account’s Google Workspace administrator can enable this ability. If you’re a Google Workspace administrator, learn how to manage access to apps in Gemini.
  • Have Keep Activity on. Only your account’s Google Workspace administrator can manage these settings. Learn more about Gemini Apps Activity settings for work or school accounts.

Important: For now, the Google Classroom app is:

  • Only available in English.
  • Only available in the Gemini mobile app and the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com.
  • Not available in certain features, like Gems or Live chats.

Are you experiencing errors? Please check with your Google Workspace administrator that access to apps in Gemini are enabled. If it is, check that the Google Classroom app is turned on in your Connected Apps settings. Learn more about Connected Apps with work and school accounts.

Connect Google Classroom to Gemini Apps

Important: If you’re signed in to a school account, the ability to connect Google Classroom app with Gemini is enabled by default unless your admin disabled it.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Ask Gemini to get information from Google Classroom, like which assignments haven’t been submitted or are due today.
    • Tip: To tell Gemini Apps to specifically use Google Classroom, add 0 to your prompt.
  3. If Google Classroom isn’t connected, you’ll get the option to connect it.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Tip: After your admin enables access, you can connect and disconnect the Google Classroom app anytime in your Connected Apps settings. If you’re a Google Workspace administrator, learn how to manage access to apps in Gemini.

What you can do as a teacher

Important: The Google Classroom connected app in Gemini Apps doesn’t support deletion, grading, or directly posting to Google Classroom.

As a teacher, you can use Gemini Apps to streamline your work in Google Classroom, track assignment submissions, inform teaching material creation, and summarize student progress. For example, you can ask Gemini to:

  • Draft communications: Draft communications and posts based on your Google Classroom information.
  • Draft differentiated assignments and plans: Help draft and update assignments, and generate timelines and structured plans, based on information and content from your Google Classroom.
  • Understand student progress and take action: Summarize who has submitted assignments, how students have done on prior assignments, and help identify where students might need additional teacher support.
  • Streamline administrative tasks: Update assignment titles, descriptions, and more across multiple classes in draft mode, make seating charts, and find old assignments.
  • Brainstorm and create activities and visual aids: Create visuals tailored to your students’ learning topics and progress, and brainstorm ideas for engaging activities for your next lesson.
  • Summarize student progress: Summarize learning progress for a specific student or a whole class of students.
  • Summarize upcoming tasks: Get a briefing of your upcoming tasks across all your classes, like assignments ready to be graded.

What you can do as a student

Important: You must be 18 or over to use the Google Classroom connected app in Gemini Apps.

As a student, you can use the Google Classroom app in Gemini Apps to help you quickly find information, check assignments details and due dates, and more. Gemini can help you:

  • Get recent assignments, due dates, and details, including:
    • A list of recent assignments.
    • Upcoming due dates.
    • Details or a summary of a particular assignment.
  • Get announcements, like recent ones or ones from a specific class.
  • Create study plans, guides, and schedules using the material from your Google Classroom.

What Gemini Apps can’t do with the Google Classroom app

Gemini Apps can’t perform certain actions in the Google Classroom app for you, like:

  • Enter grades or provide private feedback directly
  • Delete, archive, or directly post assignments or announcements
    • While Gemini cannot directly post items for you, it can post them to draft so you can review them.
  • Create rubrics

Ask for info & tailored responses using your content from Mind Space in the Gemini mobile app

You can ask the Gemini mobile app to work with your saved content in the Mind Space app on your phone, like documents, screenshots, voice notes, and more. For example, you can ask Gemini to help with the following based on your saved content:

  • Recall specific details, like your seat number from a train ticket
  • Summarize your saved content for a project
  • Help plan and create a tailored itinerary for you next trip
  • Make recommendations based on your interests and more

Important: The Mind Space connected app is designed to work automatically on supported phones, but requires certain permissions before you can use it. You can disconnect the app anytime on the Apps page in Gemini settings. Learn how to manage connected apps in Gemini.

What you need

To use the Mind Space app in the Gemini mobile app, you need to:

  • Have a supported phone running Android 16 or later. The following phones are supported: OnePlus 13s, OnePlus 15, OnePlus 15R, OPPO Find X9, and OPPO Find X9 Pro. Learn how to update your Android version.
  • Install the latest version of the Google app. Get it on Google Play.
  • Install the latest Oxygen OS 16 update.
  • Sign in to the Gemini mobile app with a personal Google Account. For now, this feature isn’t available if you sign in to a work or school Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

Important:

  • The Mind Space app isn’t available in Gemini in Google Messages or the Gemini web app.

Ask for tailored responses based on your content in Mind Space

  1. On your Android phone, open the Gemini mobile app .
  2. Ask Gemini to find info from your phone by specifying “Mind Space” in your prompt or adding 0.
  3. If the Mind Space app isn’t connected, you’ll get the option to connect it.
  4. Follow any on-screen instructions.
Examples
  • @Mind Space what’s the seat number for my train ticket for tomorrow?
  • @Mind Space what was that restaurant phone number I recorded yesterday?
  • @Mind Space Where’s my parking spot from this afternoon? What is the spot number?
  • Based on my interior design content from Mind Space, help me draft a home decor plan. [Image: After Gemini’s response:] Save this home decor plan to OnePlus Notes.
  • Can you help me plan a 5-day trip to Paris with content from my Mind Space? [Image: After Gemini’s response:] Save this travel itinerary to my OnePlus Notes.
  • Can you help me create a one-page study guide on cutting-edge Baroque architecture with content from my Mind Space? [Image: After Gemini’s response:] Save this study guide to my OnePlus Notes.

What Gemini can’t do with Mind Space

The Mind Space app in Gemini can’t:

  • Store or add new information
  • Create, manage, or delete folders
  • Add note tags
  • Invite people to shared notes or content

Broadcast messages in your home with the Gemini mobile app

Broadcast messages in your home with the Gemini mobile app

When you connect Google Home to Gemini Apps, you can ask the Gemini mobile app to broadcast messages to speakers, Smart Displays, and Smart Clocks in your home. You can broadcast to a specific device, a room, or your entire home.

What you need

To connect Google Home to Gemini Apps on an Android phone or tablet, you need to:

  • Use the Gemini mobile app, including as your mobile assistant. Learn more about the Gemini mobile app.
  • Have at least one speaker, Smart Display, or Smart Clock with Google Assistant built in.
  • Have Keep Activity on. Gemini can’t connect to Google Home when this setting is off.
  • Be signed in to the Gemini mobile app with a personal Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
    • For now, this feature isn’t available if you sign in to a work or school Google Account.
    • You must be signed in to the same account that you’re signed in to on your speaker, Smart Display, or Smart Clock.

Important:

  • For now, the Google Home app isn’t available in Gemini in Google Messages, the Gemini web app, or Live chats.
  • You can also say ‘Hey Google’ to ask Gemini to use a connected app. If “Hey Google” doesn’t work, check if “Hey Google” and Voice Match are set up.

Broadcast a message

Important: Google Home can’t broadcast to a device with “Do Not Disturb” turned on.

  1. On your phone or tablet, open the Gemini mobile app .
  2. Ask the Gemini mobile app to broadcast a message.
    • Your prompt must start with 0. You can include your message, or reply with your message in a followup prompt.
    • If you don’t specify a room or device to broadcast to, your message is broadcast to all supported devices in your home.
    • Your smart devices will use their default voice to broadcast messages.
  3. If you haven’t connected Google Home to Gemini Apps, you’ll get the option to connect it.
    • If you connect Google Home to Gemini Apps, you give Gemini permission to access and control the same homes and devices as this account in the Google Home app. This includes any homes and devices added or shared with you later.

Tip: You can connect or disconnect the Google Home app anytime in your Connected Apps settings. Learn how to manage Connected Apps in Gemini.

Example prompts
  • Broadcast a message.
  • Broadcast I’m on my way home.
  • Broadcast to the living room, it’s time for homework.
  • Find a recipe for gazpacho and broadcast it on the kitchen display.

Capture your ideas & notes with Gemini Apps

You can ask Gemini Apps to create and show your notes and lists in Google Keep, HONOR Notes, Lenovo Notes, OnePlus Notes, OPPO Notes, Samsung Notes, TECNO Notepad, vivo Notes, and Xiaomi Notes. You can also ask them to add items to existing lists in Google Keep.

What you need

To connect your notes and lists apps to Gemini Apps, you need to:

  • Be signed in to the Gemini app. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

  • Have Keep Activity on. Gemini can’t connect to these apps when this setting is off.

Important:

  • The supported notes and lists apps aren’t available in Gemini in Google Messages.
  • Gemini Apps can hallucinate responses or provide outdated information. To check the information, click and review the sources listed after the response.

Use Google Keep in Gemini Apps

To work with your notes and lists from Google Keep in Gemini Apps, Google Workspace must be connected to Gemini Apps.

  1. Go to gemini.google.com.
  2. Make sure you’re signed in to the same account you use with Google Workspace.
  3. Ask the Gemini app to create or find a list from Google Keep.
    • Tip: To tell Gemini Apps to specifically use Google Keep, add 0 to your prompt.
  4. If Google Workspace isn’t connected, you’ll get the option to connect it.
  5. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Tip: You can disconnect the Google Workspace app in your Connected Apps settings.

What Gemini Apps can’t do

Gemini Apps can’t perform certain actions in your notes and lists apps for you, like:

  • Share notes and lists
  • View images and drawings
  • Add an image

In addition, Gemini Apps can’t currently modify a note or delete notes and lists in Samsung Notes or Xiaomi notes. Gemini Apps also can’t delete a shared note owned by someone else.

Create a note or list

Create notes & lists by giving specific details

  • Create a note called [note name]
  • Create a list called [list name] with [item 1, item 2, …]

Create notes & lists based on your conversation

You can ask Gemini Apps to perform a task and create a note or list. For example:

  • Recommend some activities for [event] and save this to Keep.
  • Make an outline for [topic]. [Image: After Gemini’s response:] @Google Keep save this.
  • Tell me what steps I need to take to [goal or task]. Then create a list in Keep.
  • Find a recipe for [dish] and create a list of the ingredients in Keep.

Tips:

  • To create a note in Google Keep, you can add “Save this to Keep” or “@Google Keep save this.” Or, to create a list in Google Keep, add “Create a list in Keep” or “Create a list of the [items, steps, ingredients, …] in Keep.”
  • To create a note in another app, you can add “Save this to @[app name]” or “@[app name] save this.”

Add item to an existing list in Google Keep

Add item to an existing list

  • Add [item 1, item 2, …] to my list called [list name]
  • Include [item 1, item 2, …] to [list name] list

Tip: On supported Samsung mobile devices, the Gemini mobile app can add an item to an existing list in the Samsung Reminder app if the app is connected in your Connected Apps settings.

Add item to an existing list based on your conversation

You can ask Gemini Apps to perform a task and add an item to an existing list in Google Keep. For example:

  • What materials will I need for [activity or task]? [Image: After Gemini’s response:] Add this to my [list name] list.
  • Find me a recipe for [dish] and save the ingredients to Keep.

Tip: To undo an action, select Undo in the confirmation notification, or open and edit the list linked below the response. If you created a note with Gemini Live on in the background, Gemini can’t undo the note.

Get content from your notes & lists

Find content from your notes & lists

  • Do I have any notes related to [topic]?
  • Find my [list name] list
  • Show all my lists about [task, event, goal, …]

Use your notes & lists in your conversation

You can use your notes or lists to ask Gemini Apps to perform a task. For example:

  • Help me create a [song, story, …] based on my Keep note called [note name]
  • Suggest a [dish, activity, …] from the items in my [list name] list

Connect & manage custom apps for Gemini Spark in the Gemini web app

Connect & manage custom apps for Gemini Spark in the Gemini web app

You can connect your personal or third-party apps to build highly customized workflows with Gemini Spark in the Gemini web app. To do this, you can add any custom app with its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server URL. After you connect it in the Gemini web app, these custom Connected Apps work in Gemini Spark in both the Gemini mobile app and Gemini web app.

What you need

To connect a custom app to Gemini Apps, you must:

  • Be eligible and have access to Gemini Spark. Learn more about Gemini Spark.
  • Be 18 or over and in the US.
  • Sign in to the Gemini app with a personal Google Account. For now, this feature isn’t available if you sign in with a work or school Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.
  • Have Keep Activity on. Gemini can’t connect to custom apps when this setting is off.
  • Have the MCP server URL for the custom app. The MCP server must follow the standard MCP specifications.

Important: For now, custom Connected Apps are:

  • Only available in English.
  • Only available in Gemini Spark in the Gemini mobile app and the Gemini web app at gemini.google.com.

Before you connect a custom app

Google does not control, monitor, or secure third-party MCP servers. You’re responsible for supervising the MCP server. Make sure you understand the actions an MCP server supports and trust the provider before connecting it to Gemini Apps.

Learn more about the risks of connecting custom apps.

Connect a custom app

Important: You can only connect custom apps in the Gemini web app. Once connected, they’re available on both the Gemini mobile app and Gemini web app.

You can add a custom app by linking its MCP server in your Connected Apps settings.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.

  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help   Connected Apps .

    • If you don’t find “Connected Apps,” first click Personal Intelligence Connected Apps. Learn about Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps.

  3. Under “Custom apps for Spark,” find the “Add a custom app link to get started” field, or if you already connected a custom app, click Add a custom app .

  4. Enter the app’s MCP server URL.

    • If the server doesn’t support Dynamic Client Registration, next to “Advanced features,” click Show more, then enter your credentials.

  5. Click Next.

  6. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Disconnect a custom app

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.

  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help   Connected Apps .

    • If you don’t find “Connected Apps,” first click Personal Intelligence Connected Apps. Learn about Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps.

  3. Under “Custom apps for Spark,” find the app you want to disconnect and turn it off .

  4. Follow any on-screen instructions.

Unlink an MCP server from your Google Account

You can unlink an MCP server from your Google Account and revoke its permissions in your Connected Apps settings. This also disconnects the custom app so that Gemini can’t use it, but doesn’t remove it from your Connected Apps settings. You can reconnect the custom app anytime by relinking the MCP server.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.

  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help   Connected Apps .

    • If you don’t find “Connected Apps,” first click Personal Intelligence Connected Apps. Learn about Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps.

  3. Under “Custom apps for Spark,” find the custom app that you want to disconnect.

  4. Click More details Disconnect.

Tip: You can also unlink an MCP server from your Google Account’s Linked apps page. Learn how to manage linked apps.

Remove a custom connected app

If you no longer want Gemini to use a custom connected app, you can remove it. When you remove a custom app, it also unlinks the MCP server from your Google Account.

  1. On your computer, go to gemini.google.com.

  2. At the bottom, click Settings & help   Connected Apps .

    • If you don’t find “Connected Apps,” first click Personal Intelligence Connected Apps. Learn about Personal Intelligence and Connected Apps.

  3. Under “Custom apps for Spark,” find the custom app that you want to remove.

  4. Click More details Remove app.

  5. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Understand risks of connecting custom Connected Apps

Custom third-party Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, or custom connected apps, extend Gemini’s capabilities. But, it’s important to understand the associated risks and data privacy considerations:

  • Outside Google’s control: Google does not control, monitor, or secure custom third-party MCP servers. After your data leaves Gemini and is sent to a custom connected app, it’s subject to that app’s privacy practices. Currently, Gemini requires manual confirmation for any write actions, but Gemini can make mistakes. This is why it’s very important that you know and trust the custom third-party MCP server before connecting.
  • Your responsibility: Because custom third-party MCP servers operate outside of Google’s control, we recommend that you do not connect them unless you trust the underlying application. Supervise these closely. Always verify that you trust the provider and review their Privacy Policy and Terms of Service, which explain how they will use your data, before connecting.
  • Excessive data requests: Custom apps may request data beyond what is strictly needed for your request. This can include data you consider sensitive so pay attention to what data is being written into these servers.
  • Data sharing: When you use a custom connected app, Gemini may share information from your chat and other available sources, like Connected Apps, Personal Intelligence, skills, tasks, and logged-in websites. This introduces risks of unintended data exposure or unauthorized account access, even for servers that are not malicious.

What you can do to protect your data

  • Thoroughly review: Make sure you trust the third-party. Read the app’s Privacy Policy, Terms of Service, and available documentation before connecting so that you understand how it works.
  • Monitor and remove: Regularly review your custom Connected Apps. If you no longer need a custom connected app, disconnect and remove it from Gemini to revoke access.

Learn how Google helps you share data safely using Google Account Linking.

For more general privacy information, review the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub.

Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps

Connect the Google Workspace app to Gemini Apps

In Gemini Apps, you can use the Google Workspace app to connect with your data in Google Workspace services to improve your productivity and streamline your workflows. With the Google Workspace app, you can ask Gemini Apps to:

  • Summarize, get quick answers, and find information from Google Workspace services like Gmail, Docs, and Drive
  • Add, edit, and get your tasks and reminders from Google Tasks
  • Create and get your notes and lists from Google Keep
  • Create & manage your events in Google Calendar

Tip: You can also get personalized Gemini experiences based on your content in Gmail when you connect the Google Workspace app. Learn more about personalization based on Connected Apps.

What you need

To connect Google Workspace to Gemini Apps, you need to:

  • Be signed in to the Gemini app. Make sure you sign in to the same account you use with Google Workspace. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

  • Have Keep Activity on. Gemini can’t connect to Google Workspace when this setting is off.

Important:

  • For now, only some Google Workspace services are available in Live chats. Learn how to use Connected Apps in Live chats.
  • Gemini Apps can hallucinate responses or provide outdated information, like from an older email when there’s a more recent one. To check the information, select and review the sources listed after the response.

Use the Google Workspace app in Gemini Apps

  1. Make sure you’re signed in to the same account you use with Google Workspace.
  2. Ask the Gemini app to get information from Google Workspace.
    • Tip: Don’t paste the URL of a document or email in your prompt. To reference content in Google Workspace, use keywords from the content and specify the service or content type. To specify a Google Workspace service, enter 0 and select the service.
  3. If you haven’t connected Google Workspace, you’ll get the option to connect it.
  4. Follow the on-screen instructions.

You can disconnect the Google Workspace app in your Connected Apps settings.

Examples
  • Find information
    • What dates did Erik propose in the email about the Grand Canyon hiking trip?
    • Find the most recent lease agreement from my Drive and check how much the security deposit was
  • Summarize a document
    • Find my resume titled June 2023 from my drive and summarize it to a short paragraph personal statement
  • Simplify and organize information
    • Find the doc from Ashley about the neighborhood clean-up project and summarize the proposal for me in 5 bullets
  • Capture tasks from your conversation to Google Tasks
    • Help me plan a camping trip and create a packing list for me. [Image: After Gemini’s response:] Create a reminder to bring those things in Tasks.
  • Save ideas & notes to Google Keep
    • Recommend some places to visit in Kyoto and save them to Keep.
    • Find me a recipe for apple pie and save the ingredients to Keep.
  • Check your schedule & manage Calendar events
    • What’s on my calendar today?
    • Check the email that Alice sent about our trip to Tahoe this weekend, and add it to my calendar.

Why can’t I connect the Google Workspace app

For work and school accounts, the Google Workspace administrator must first enable the ability to connect with apps. Learn how to connect to apps in Gemini with a work or school account.

Required settings in Gmail might be turned off. For Gemini Apps to connect with Google Workspace, Smart features in other Google products must be turned on in your Gmail settings. If you turn this on, reload the Gemini app and try to connect again.

Learn how to change smart features and personalization settings.

Mention the Google Workspace app or a Google Workspace service in your prompt. For every new conversation, ask the Gemini app to get or add something from your personal Google Workspace explicitly. You can mention Gmail or email, Docs or documents, Drive or PDFs, events or Calendar, to-dos or Tasks, and notes or Keep in your prompt. You don’t need to do this for follow up questions in the same chat. For example:

  • First prompt: Summarize my recent emails from Harper elementary school
  • Next prompt: When is pajama day?

What Gemini Apps can’t do with the Google Workspace app

Gemini Apps can’t:

  • Access comments or images in Docs or Gmail
  • Access pictures and videos in your Drive
    • This includes any content that isn’t in a document, spreadsheet, presentation, or PDF
  • Create, draft, or delete spreadsheets, PDFs, documents, and presentations
  • Manage content in your Drive, like create folders or move content between folders
  • Count items in your Drive or Gmail or tell you how much Drive or Gmail storage you have
