Gemini Apps limits & upgrades

Gemini Apps has usage limits designed to ensure an optimal experience for everyone. This means we may at times have to cap the number of prompts and conversations you can have, or how much you can use some features, within a specific timeframe.

The number of prompts you can use before hitting the limit varies and depends on factors like how long and complex your prompts are, the size and number of files you upload, and the length of your conversations with Gemini Apps.

Your capacity replenishes regularly, so you can get back to chatting with Gemini Apps soon, or you can upgrade to a higher plan.

What is a context window?

What is a context window?

When you upload files to Gemini Apps, it needs to “read” the content to provide useful insights or answers. The context window is like the reading capacity. It determines how much content can be understood together at one time.

Why you might want a larger context window

A larger context window allows Gemini to read and comprehend more. For example, with a 1M token context window, Gemini can understand up to 1,500 pages of text or 30,000 lines of code.

If you exceed the context window, this could lead to responses that don’t take into account all the content provided or miss connections or details throughout the content. This is most relevant for prompts that require attention to many details scattered throughout large files.

Ask Gemini in Chrome to complete tasks for you with auto browse

Ask Gemini in Chrome to complete tasks for you with auto browse

With auto browse, you can ask Gemini in Chrome to complete multi-step tasks for you on the web. Your preferences, instructions, and previously shared details are reviewed to help you receive personalized, useful results. For example, you can ask it to:

  • Compare products, search for deals, and add items to your cart
  • Help you find and book travel accommodations based on specific criteria
  • Make restaurant reservations and schedule appointments
  • Help you with many more tasks

What you need

To use auto browse on your computer, you need to:

  • Be 18 or over and in the US.
  • Be eligible and opt in to Gemini in Chrome. Learn how to get Gemini in Chrome.
  • Update to the latest version of Chrome. Learn how to update Chrome.
  • Set your device’s language to English.
  • Have Google AI Ultra or Google AI Pro on your personal account. Learn how to upgrade.
  • Sign in to Chrome with a personal Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Chrome.
    • This feature isn’t available in Incognito mode. It’s also not available if you sign in to Chrome with a school Google Account.
  • In Chrome, set “Safe Browsing” to Enhanced or Standard protection. Learn how to change your protection settings.

Important:

  • We’re gradually releasing auto browse in Gemini in Chrome, so it might not be available to you just yet.
  • For now, this feature is not available in Live chats or Gemini in Chrome on iPhone or iPad.

Ask Gemini in Chrome to complete tasks for you

Important: Gemini in Chrome can use a broad range of sites on the web to complete tasks for you. This is true even if you haven’t connected the related apps to Gemini Apps. Learn more about connected apps.

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the text box, describe the task you want it to complete.
  4. Click Submit .
  5. Review the plan Gemini in Chrome will use to complete the task.
    • Check that it understood your prompt, the page context, and your personal info correctly.
    • Note: Gemini will choose which sites to use to complete the task, and it may share your personal info with those sites.
  6. If the plan is correct, click Start Task.
    • While Gemini in Chrome is performing the task, there’s an auto browse icon on the tab that it’s using.
    • When Gemini in Chrome needs you to complete a step, you’ll get a notification at the top of your browser.
  7. If needed to complete a task:
    • Review and confirm any sensitive steps.
    • Take over a task for steps you need to complete personally.
    • Give Gemini in Chrome permission to sign in to a site for you.

Tips:

  • To go to the task tab: Next to the task in the chat, click Switch tabs.
    • If a task needs your attention, at the top of your browser, click Check your task.
  • To take over a task from Gemini in Chrome: On the task tab, click Take over task .
  • To resume a task: In Gemini in Chrome, click Resume or Give back task.
  • To stop a task: In Gemini in Chrome, click Stop . You can also close the task tab.
  • Learn how to report a problem or send feedback about Gemini in Chrome.
Examples

You can ask Gemini in Chrome to:

  • Find and book travel accommodations based on specific criteria
  • Manage dining reservations and food delivery
  • Search for tickets for events and group entertainment
  • Find and compare products for online shopping
  • Draft communications and organize calendar schedules
  • Research job markets and professional networking opportunities
  • Assist with online finance chores like fetching receipts
  • Perform other administrative web tasks

Take over a task

While Gemini in Chrome is performing a task, you can take over the task at any time. For certain tasks that you need to complete personally, Gemini will ask you to take over.

To take over a task:

  1. Go to the tab that Gemini in Chrome is using for the task.
  2. Click Take over task .
  3. Complete the steps you want to do yourself or Gemini asked you to do.
  4. To give back the task, in the Gemini in Chrome chat, click Resume or Give back task.

Manage sites that Gemini in Chrome signs you in to

With your permission, Gemini in Chrome can get help from Google Password Manager to sign in to sites for you. Google Password Manager does not share your passwords with Gemini in Chrome. You can remove this permission at any time.

To remove permission for Gemini in Chrome to sign in to a site for you:

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top right, click More Passwords and autofill Google Password Manager.
  3. On the left, click Settings.
  4. Under “Gemini can sign in for you,” review sites that you’ve allowed Gemini to automatically sign in to.
  5. To remove a site, click Delete .

Change whether Gemini in Chrome can browse for you

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top, click More Settings.
  3. In the Settings menu, click AI innovations Gemini in Chrome .
    • If the menu is hidden, first click Menu .
  4. Under “Permissions,” turn Let Gemini browse for you off or on.

About Gemini in Chrome’s limits

In Gemini in Chrome, there are limits for the number of:

  • Multi-step tasks that you can request each day
    • With a Google AI Pro plan: up to 20 requests per day
    • With a Google AI Ultra plan: up to 200 requests per day
  • Multi-step tasks that Gemini in Chrome can perform at the same time

When you reach your limit, Gemini in Chrome lets you know.

How Gemini in Chrome works with you to keep you & your info safe

Gemini in Chrome working as an agent is an experimental feature. As we continuously work to improve its safeguards, use auto browse in Gemini in Chrome carefully and safely to prevent unintended and potentially harmful results. You’re responsible for Gemini’s actions during a task, including mistakes and unexpected results like purchases.

About possible risks of using AI agents

AI agents, like auto browse in Gemini in Chrome, are helpful and powerful tools, but it’s important to be aware of possible risks. Remember that Gemini in Chrome can make mistakes and do unexpected things.

About prompt injection

Prompt injection is an attempt to elicit an unintended or harmful response from generative AI tools like Gemini in Chrome. This happens when content, like a website, an email, a document, or multimedia, has malicious instructions that might be hidden from you but visible to the AI agent.

If an AI agent reads these instructions while doing a task, it might be tricked into doing unintended things. For example, a malicious instruction could tell the agent to:

  • Take your private info from your emails or documents and post it on a public website
  • Send your emails in Gmail to an external service without you knowing
  • Expose insights about you based on your data in connected apps
Gemini in Chrome can share your info with websites

Auto-browse works across your open tabs to complete actions and get things done on your behalf. Gemini can choose sites to visit to fulfill your request. Gemini may use your personal information (such as data from Connected Apps like Google Workspace) to complete these tasks more accurately. When completing an auto browse task on a website, Gemini may share your information with that site.

Note: You can manage your data-sharing preferences and Connected Apps in your Gemini settings.

Gemini in Chrome can make mistakes

Gemini in Chrome might misunderstand what you want it to do or the website it’s browsing. This could lead to unintended actions, like:

  • Following instructions incorrectly or clicking the wrong link or button
  • Completing a purchase or ordering something without your permission
  • Adding the wrong quantity of an item to your cart or forgetting to add an item
  • Confirming a task is done when it’s not or could have done more
  • Asking you to take over when it can normally do the step

Learn about how we address these risks in Gemini in Chrome.

How Gemini in Chrome was designed to keep you & your info safe

Chrome has safeguards for auto browse that aim to reduce the possible risks of AI agents, including unintended or potentially harmful actions. While these do not guarantee protection against all risks, these safeguards include:

  • “Take over task”: Gemini in Chrome may ask you to take over the task to complete specific actions, like:
    • Finalizing financial transactions
    • Accepting terms of service
    • Creating an account
  • Requests for user confirmation: Gemini in Chrome aims to ask for your review and confirmation before certain actions, like:
    • Starting a task
    • Sending communications
    • Modifying your data
    • Submitting web forms
    • Scheduling events
    • Accessing sites with highly sensitive financial or health data
  • Requests for permission: Gemini in Chrome asks for your permission before it gets help from Google Password Manager to sign in to sites for you. Google Password Manager does not share your passwords with Gemini in Chrome. You can remove this permission at any time.
  • Prohibited task recognition: Gemini in Chrome has safeguards designed to help it recognize and not act on certain types of requests that could be harmful or are outside of its intended purpose, including tasks that may violate the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.
  • Site & action restrictions: Gemini in Chrome restricts its activity to the websites and actions relevant to your task. This helps protect your data on other unrelated sites and helps prevent actions that don’t align with your task. These are just some ways we protect against prompt injection.

Learn more about the safeguards in Chrome for auto browse.

Why monitoring your tasks is important & how to stop Gemini in Chrome

Chrome’s safeguards for auto browse described above don’t guarantee protection against all risks.

Monitor important & sensitive tasks

Monitoring your tasks is the most important way to protect against risk while using auto browse. Review confirmation requests and clarifying questions closely. Use auto browse carefully and safely, and only give Gemini in Chrome tasks you’re comfortable with. Be extra watchful when Gemini in Chrome:

  • Handles an important task
  • Is signed in to websites with sensitive info, like financial, legal, and medical info
  • Does anything where a mistake could be a problem
  • Uses Connected apps, like Google Workspace, in the same chat
You’re in control

If Gemini in Chrome is doing something you don’t like, you can stop it by clicking Stop in Gemini in Chrome or Take over task on the tab that Gemini in Chrome is using. Gemini in Chrome’s safeguards aren’t intended to replace your monitoring.

About your data & Gemini in Chrome

You can review your chats with Gemini in Chrome in Gemini Apps Activity. Learn how to manage and delete your Gemini Apps activity.

You can review the sites Gemini in Chrome visits in your Chrome history. These sites have Gemini action icon next to them. Learn how to check and delete your Chrome browsing history.

Learn more about what happens to your data when you use Gemini in Chrome.

Chat with Gemini in your car

Chat with Gemini in your car

When you connect your phone to your car with Android Auto, you can use your voice to chat with Gemini to get things done. With Gemini as your driving co-pilot, you can do things like:

  • Place calls and send text messages
  • Find places and start navigation
  • Start, stop, and change your music
  • Have a back-and-forth conversation with Gemini

What you need to connect to Gemini in Android Auto

On Android Auto from your phone:
  • An Android phone with at least 2 GB of RAM, running Android 11 or newer
  • Gemini set as your digital assistant. Learn how to get started with Gemini.
  • A vehicle that supports Android Auto. Learn how to connect your phone with Android Auto.
For a vehicle with Google built-in:
  • A vehicle with Google built-in.
  • A Google Account signed in to your vehicle.
  • Gemini enabled as your assistant in the vehicle’s settings. To enable Gemini:
    1. On your car’s screen, tap Settings Google Assistant.
    2. Select Gemini [icon] as your digital assistant.
    3. If Gemini is not listed, ensure your vehicle’s software is up to date.

Gemini and Android Auto are not available in all languages and regions. Find where Gemini is supported and where Android Auto is supported.

Chat with Gemini

When your phone is connected to your vehicle, to start a chat with Gemini:

  • Say “Hey Google”
    • “Hey Google” only works when Voice Match and “Hey Google” are turned on. Learn more about Voice Match and “Hey Google.”
  • On your car’s screen, tap Microphone
  • If available, press and hold the voice command button on your steering wheel until Gemini activates

Then, say what you want Gemini to help you with. For example, try saying, “Hey Google, call Mom.” Gemini can also help with more complex tasks. Try asking, “Hey Google, find a supercharger near a sushi restaurant that’s open now.”

Chat Live with Gemini

You can have a free-flowing, natural conversation with Gemini when you tap Microphone on the screen and say, “Let’s talk Live.” When you chat Live with Gemini in your car, you can do things like:

  • Discuss a topic that interests you, like music artists or quantum theory.
  • Ask Gemini for entertainment, like trivia questions, jokes, or help finding a podcast.
  • Get travel info, like discussing a destination or asking about landmarks you pass by.

Tip: To stop your Live conversation, say “Stop.” For now, you can only start and stop Live with your voice.

Using Gemini for Android Auto with children

When you use Gemini with Android Auto, Gemini is available to anyone in the vehicle, including children. This means that children in the vehicle may hear content that may be age inappropriate.

Gemini is conversational and can feel like a human. It’s important to remind any children in the vehicle that Gemini is an AI tool, not a person. Learn more about guiding your child’s Gemini Apps experience.

Gemini in Android Auto is new and evolving, and can hallucinate and present inaccurate information as factual so should not be relied on for critical information or safety-related matters while operating the vehicle.

Customize your Gemini in Chrome experience

Customize your Gemini in Chrome experience

You can tailor different elements of Gemini in Chrome to better reflect your style, preferences, and personal needs. Change the way Gemini sounds, how you interact with it, the services it can connect to, and more.

Important: Gemini in Chrome is not available to all users at this time. We’re gradually releasing Gemini in Chrome, so it might not be available to you just yet.

  • See the regions where Gemini in Chrome is available.
  • Check the languages that Gemini in Chrome supports.

Use skills in Gemini in Chrome to complete tasks faster

When you find a useful AI prompt – like asking Gemini to calculate protein macros for a recipe or to compare product specifications across multiple tabs – you don’t need to type it from scratch on a new page to try it again. Use Skills in Chrome to save your most helpful prompts and run them with a single click on any page you visit.

A skill works directly with the page you currently see. When you use a skill, Gemini in Chrome reads the content on your active tab and applies your saved instructions to it. You can also discover and remix ready-to-use skills from a built-in library.

Here are some examples:

  • Protein max: Change a standard recipe by inserting high-protein substitutes wherever possible.
  • Check job fit: Analyze a job description against your background and resume to help figure out if you’re a good fit for the role and highlight important experiences.
  • Explain simply: Translate the complicated text you’re reading using simpler terms and analogies that even a kindergartener could understand.

What you need

To use Skills in Gemini in Chrome, you need to:

  • Use a Chromebook Plus, Mac, or Windows computer.
  • Use the latest version of Chrome. Learn how to check your browser version.
  • Have Gemini in Chrome turned on.
  • Sign in with a personal Google Account
  • Use Gemini in Chrome with your Chrome language set to English (United States).
  • Be 13 or older (or the applicable age in your country) and in a supported region.

Note: Skills are not currently available for managed or Enterprise accounts unless your organization’s administrator has enabled the feature.

Skills are currently rolling out gradually. If you don’t see this feature yet, you can turn it on manually:

  1. Check that you’re on Chrome version 147 or higher by typing chrome://version into your address bar.
  2. Go to chrome://flags and search for “Skills.” Enable the Skills flag.
  3. Relaunch Chrome.
  4. Open the Gemini side panel and type / to confirm skills are available.

Browse recommended skills in Gemini in Chrome

There are several skills already built into Gemini in Chrome for you to try.

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the text box, type a forward slash (/) to open the Skills menu.
  4. Scroll to browse available skills.
    1. Tip: Hover over a skill to learn what it will do.
  5. Click to select the skill you want.
  6. Press Enter or click Send.

For an expanded list of all available skills, type chrome://skills/browse into your address bar. You can filter by skill type or search by name.

Make your own skills in Gemini in Chrome

You can also come up with your own skills to use in the future. You can add as many custom skills as you like.

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the text box, type a forward slash (/) to open the Skills menu.
  4. Click Add Skill +.
  5. Fill in the popup with a name and prompt for the skill you want to create.
  6. Click Save.

If you open Gemini in Chrome and want to use that skill again, type “/” followed by the name of your custom skill.

Manage your available skills

You can make changes to the skills you made, changing their behavior or deleting them if no longer useful.

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the text box, type a forward slash (/) to open the Skills menu.
  4. At the bottom of the Skills menu, click Browse Skills 🧭.
  5. Decide what you want to do:
    1. Change an existing skill: click Edit
    2. Create a new skill: at the top, click + Add.
    3. Delete a skill: at the top ofthe skill you want to remove, click More > Delete.

Tips:

  • To reach the Skills page directly, in your address bar, type chrome://skills/yourSkills.
  • To quickly reuse a skill’s text, at the top, click More > Copy Instructions.
  • In the Edit skill popup, to make your instructions more robust, click the pencil icon.

Use Connected Apps in Gemini in Chrome

Important: Only some Connected Apps are available in Gemini in Chrome. Learn about which apps Gemini in Chrome can connect to.

If you connect the Google Workspace app, Gemini in Chrome can help you get things done with Google Workspace services, like:

  • Summarize your emails in Gmail
  • Add items to Google Tasks
  • Create events in Google Calendar

Learn more:

  • About Connected Apps in Gemini Apps.
  • About personalization with Connected Apps.

Apps that Gemini in Chrome can connect to

Note: In some countries, Connected Apps do not use Personal Intelligence to tailor your answer.

Gemini in Chrome can currently connect to the following apps:

  • Google Workspace, which includes:
    • Gmail
    • Google Calendar
    • Google Docs
    • Google Drive
    • Google Keep
    • Google Tasks
  • Google Photos

Manage your experience with Connected Apps

You can connect and disconnect apps from Gemini Apps at any time in your Connected Apps settings.

Important: You can learn more about your data and Connected Apps in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub:

  • What happens when you disconnect an app in Gemini
  • How your data is handled when you use Connected Apps in Gemini

To disconnect or connect apps:

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. At the top of Gemini in Chrome, click More  Settings & help Personal Intelligence Connected Apps.
  4. Find the app you want and turn it off or on .
    • This disconnects or connects an app for all Gemini Apps, including Gemini in Chrome.
    • Only some Connected Apps are available in Gemini in Chrome. Learn about which apps Gemini in Chrome can connect to.
  5. Follow any on-screen instructions.

Manage Connected Apps

Services that Gemini in Chrome automatically uses

In addition to Connected Apps, Gemini in Chrome can also automatically use public information from certain Google services to provide more helpful responses to your prompts. For example, Gemini in Chrome can help you:

  • Find relevant YouTube videos and answer questions you have about the video
  • Get location-based information from Google Maps

Currently, Gemini in Chrome automatically uses public information from these Google services:

  • Google Search
  • Google Maps
  • YouTube
  • Google Travel (Flights and Hotel searches)

To use public information from Google Maps and YouTube, Keep Activity must be on. Gemini in Chrome can always use public information from Google Search, even if Keep Activity is off.

Use Personal Intelligence with Gemini in Chrome

With their permission, eligible users with Personal Intelligence can connect their data in some Google apps to Gemini in Chrome to get new, more personalized experiences previously unavailable through Connected Apps. By combining personal content with the context of the webpage, Gemini provides more personalized assistance.

  • Learn more about Gemini eligibility.
  • Learn more about personalization with Connected Apps.

To use personalization in Gemini in Chrome:

  • You must be 18 or over and in Canada, India, New Zealand, or the US.
  • Set your device settings to use a supported language.
  • Personalization isn’t available in Gemini Live.

Set Up Personalization

Manage your personal info and preferences

At any time, you can manage how your personal info is used to tailor responses and share insights.

  • To stop personalization based on your past chats, turn off Memory in Gemini settings. Learn how to manage your past Gemini chats.
  • To stop using info from other apps, like Photos and Gmail, manage your Connected Apps in Gemini.

Use or customize keyboard shortcuts

After you opt in to using Gemini in Chrome, you can use keyboard shortcuts.

To open or close Gemini in Chrome:

  • On Mac, press Ctrl + G
  • On Windows, press Alt + G
  • On ChromeOS, press Search + G

To switch between your tab and Gemini in Chrome:

  • On Mac, press Ctrl + ⌘ + G
  • On Windows, press Alt + Shift + G
  • On ChromeOS, press Search + Alt + G

To start selection mode in Gemini in Chrome:

  • On Mac, press Ctrl + Shift + G
  • On Windows, press Ctrl + Alt + G
  • On ChromeOS, press Ctrl + Shift + G
Change the keyboard shortcuts

To choose your own keyboard shortcuts:

  1. At the top of Gemini in Chrome, click More options Settings & help Open Chrome settings.
  2. Next to the keyboard or navigation shortcut, click Edit .
  3. On your keyboard, press the new shortcut.

Change the voice used by Gemini Live

The first time you turn on Gemini Live while using Gemini in Chrome, you’ll pick a voice that’s used for responses. If you want to switch to another voice later:

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini in Chrome .
  3. In the text box, click Go Live .
    1. If necessary, click OK to confirm you want to start using Gemini Live.
  4. Change Gemini’s voice: at the top, click More options Select Voice .

Edit images from the web in Gemini in Chrome

Edit images from the web in Gemini in Chrome

You can transform any image on the internet with Gemini in Chrome.

What you need

To edit images from the web in Gemini in Chrome on your computer:

  • Opt in to Gemini in Chrome. Learn how to get Gemini in Chrome.

  • Use the latest version of Chrome. Learn how to update Chrome.

  • Sign in to Chrome. This feature isn’t available in Incognito mode. Learn how to sign in to Chrome.

  • To generate images, you must be 13 (or the applicable age in your country) or over.

  • To edit images, you must be 18 or over.

Important:

  • We’re gradually releasing this feature, so it may not be available to you just yet.
  • For now, this feature isn’t available if you’re signed in to a work or school Google Account.
  • If you want to create images tailored entirely to you, learn how to generate personalized images with Gemini Apps.

Before you use this feature

When you generate images with Gemini Apps, remember that you agreed to Google’s Terms of Service, including the Prohibited Use Policy. Be sure not to violate others’ copyright or privacy rights. Use your discretion before you rely on, publish, or use content that Gemini Apps generate. Users with a work or school account may be subject to different terms depending on the license type. Learn more about how to use Gemini Apps with your work or school Google Account.

Edit images with Nano Banana

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. Find an image you want to edit.
  3. Right click the image Create image with Gemini.
    • If you don’t find “Create image with Gemini” for a specific image, the image might be protected or not supported.
  4. In Gemini in Chrome, describe the image you want to create or select a suggestion.

Tip: To save or copy the generated image, right click the image Save image as… or Copy image.

Examples
  • Reimagine this photo without any people in the background.
  • Reimagine this photo of my handmade mug as a professional product shot.
  • Reimagine this photo to remove the small scratch on my grandchild’s face.
  • Reimagine this photo to make this hand-drawn sketch into a vectorized logo.

Tips for image generation prompts

  • Start your prompt with words like draw, generate, and create.
  • Describe the image style you want. Here are a few examples: photorealistic, charcoal drawing, watercolor painting, cartoon illustration.
  • Include a detailed visual description of what you want in the image. This can include the subject of the image, what the subject is doing, and the background or setting.

Go Live with Gemini in Chrome

Go Live with Gemini in Chrome

On a computer, you can go Live and talk naturally with Gemini in Chrome while you browse web pages. With Gemini Live, you can do things like: ask questions to learn more about a topic, brainstorm ideas, or get help finding info on a page. You can interrupt the conversation to add more details or change topics.

What you need

To go Live with Gemini in Chrome on a computer, you need to:

  • Opt in to Gemini in Chrome. Learn how to get Gemini in Chrome.
  • Use the latest version of Chrome. Learn how to update Chrome.
  • Allow access to your device’s microphone and speaker. Learn how to use your microphone in Chrome.

Go Live with Gemini in Chrome

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the text box, click Go Live .
  4. For your first time, follow the on-screen instructions to set up Gemini Live.
  5. Start talking. You can even interrupt mid-response when you want to add more details or change the topic.

Learn more about how Google works with Gemini Live data.

Manage your Live chat with Gemini in Chrome

In Gemini in Chrome, you can:

  • Turn closed captions on or off: at the top, click Turn on live captions or Turn off live captions .
  • To continue chat with text: at the bottom, click Switch to text mode .
  • Start a new chat: at the top, click More options Start New Chat .
  • Change Gemini’s voice: at the top, click More options Select Voice .

Manage permissions for Gemini in Chrome

To go Live, make sure Gemini in Chrome has permission to use page content in Chrome and your device’s microphone.

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top, click More Settings.
  3. In the Settings menu, click AI innovations Gemini in Chrome .
    • If the menu is hidden, first click Menu .
  4. Under “Permissions,” you can turn the following permissions on or off:
    • Precise location
    • Microphone
      • Users under 18 can’t turn on the Microphone or Closed Captions.
    • Share current tab by default
    • Let Gemini browse for you
      • ****Users under 18 can’t use auto browse.

Manage tabs shared with Gemini Live

Share or pause sharing your current tab

If you share your current tab and go to a different page on your current tab, Gemini uses the new page. You can pause sharing your current tab at any time. Learn how Gemini in Chrome works with your data.

  • To share your current tab: In Gemini Live, click Share current tab .
    • This shares the page content from the tab you’re on, and Gemini uses it to respond.
    • When Gemini is using a page, the page’s edges glow and its tab shows a glowing underline.
  • To pause sharing your current tab: In Gemini Live, click Current tab or Pause sharing current tab .
    • When a tab is no longer shared, the glow from the page’s edges and the glowing underline on the tab disappears.

Share or stop sharing other open tabs

In addition to your current tab, you can share up to 10 of your recent open tabs across your browser windows. You can share these tabs in the Gemini Live window. Learn how Gemini in Chrome works with your data.

To manage shared tabs:

  1. In Gemini Live, click Add tabs .
    • If you already shared other tabs, click the Manage tabs button, which shows the number of currently shared tabs.
  2. Next to the tab you want to share, click Add tab .
    • To remove a tab, click Remove tab .

To remove all shared tabs: on the Manage tabs button, click Stop sharing tabs .

Navigate web pages with your voice

Important:

  • We’re gradually releasing this feature, so it might not be available to you just yet.
  • To use this feature, you need to turn on Page content sharing and Microphone permissions. Learn how to manage permissions.

While you’re Live with Gemini in Chrome, you can use your voice to navigate the web page on your current tab. You can ask Gemini to do things like scroll to and highlight relevant content.

For example, you can use Live to help you:

  • Find info quickly. Ask Gemini to find specific info to help you answer a homework question or scroll to gluten-free recipes in a long list of recipes.
  • Follow instructions hands-free. Ask Gemini to go to the next step while working on a messy craft project.

To navigate a web page with your voice:

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the text box, click Go Live .
  4. Use your voice to ask Gemini to navigate the specific content on the current web page.
    • You can say “Scroll me,” “Go to,” or “Take me to”.
    • Gemini can’t navigate PDFs by voice.

Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products

Learn about smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products

To give you more granular control over your data, we’ve updated our smart feature settings for Google Workspace. This update turns the existing control into two distinct settings that govern different product experiences. These updates also give you more choice and control over your data, and do not alter our underlying data handling practices or our robust privacy commitments.

In Calendar, Chat, Drive, Gmail, Meet, and Voice, you can manage smart feature settings. Depending on your smart feature settings, you can do things like:

  • Use Gemini in Google Workspace to reference Drive files from Gmail.
  • Automatically add events such as flights from Gmail to Calendar.
  • Compile loyalty cards and tickets from your inbox into Google Wallet.
  • Track an upcoming order using summary cards in Gmail.
  • Record, transcribe, and summarize notes in Meet and Voice.
Smart features & controls for Google Workspace & other Google products
In this article
  • Learn about smart feature settings & experiences
  • Learn how smart features use your Google Workspace content & activity
  • Change smart feature settings
  • Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings

Learn about smart feature settings & experiences

Each Workspace smart feature setting works independently from one another and provides different experiences. For example, you can turn on smart features for Google Workspace, and turn off smart features for other Google products. To understand how each smart feature setting works, use the table below.

  • Smart feature setting: Smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet; Where to find the setting: Gmail; Description: Controls use of your Gmail, Chat, and Meet data to provide smart features for these products.; Experience example: Smart Compose in Gmail Summary cards
  • Smart feature setting: Smart features in Google Workspace; Where to find the setting: Gmail Calendar* Chat* Drive* Meet* Voice*; Description: Controls use of your Workspace data to provide smart features across Workspace products. This setting does not affect smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, which are subject to the control described above.; Experience example: Show events from Gmail in Calendar, such as flight itineraries and invitations Google Workspace with Gemini
  • Smart feature setting: Smart features in other Google products; Where to find the setting: Gmail Calendar* Chat* Drive* Meet* Voice*; Description: Controls use of your Workspace data to provide smart features in other Google products. Data sharing and personalization in certain Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).; Experience example: Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only) Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)

* You can only turn on this setting from a web browser.

Smart features in Gmail, Chat & Meet

When you turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, you agree to let Gmail, Chat and Meet use your content and activity in these products to personalize your experience in those apps.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in Gmail, Chat and Meet that include:

  • Automatic email filtering / categorization (Primary/Social/Promotions)
  • Smart Compose (suggested text) in email
  • Smart Reply (suggested quick replies) in email
  • Summary cards above emails (travel, package tracking, and more)

The setting controls app-level smart features which personalize your experience within Gmail, Chat, or Meet. Changes to this setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Google Workspace setting.

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Gmail, Chat, and Meet. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Even if you turn off smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet, some smart features with individual on and off settings are still available. Some examples include:

  • Conversation summaries in Chat
  • Smart Reply in Chat

Smart features in Google Workspace

When you turn on smart features in Google Workspace, you agree to let Google Workspace use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience across Workspace. Workspace includes apps for businesses and schools, such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more. To learn more, visit the Workspace website.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences across Workspace that include:

  • Show events from Gmail in Calendar (such as flight itineraries and invitations).
  • Personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results) in products like Drive.
  • Ask Gemini to summarize content, create drafts, and find key information, along with other Google Workspace with Gemini features.

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in Google Workspace products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

Changes to the smart features in Google Workspace setting don’t affect your existing control over the smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet setting described above.

Smart features in other Google products

When you turn on smart features in other Google products, you agree to let Google use your Workspace content and activity to personalize your experience in other Google products.

When you turn this setting on, you can get experiences in other Google products that include:

  • Restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps (personal accounts only)
  • Suggested tickets, passes and loyalty cards in Wallet (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in the Gemini app (personal accounts only)
  • Personal Intelligence in Search services (personal accounts only)

When you turn off this setting, you can’t use the experiences listed above in other Google products. To continue to use these experiences, you need to turn the setting back on.

In addition, data sharing and personalization in other Google products may be subject to additional controls, such as Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).

Even when the setting for smart features in other Google products is turned off, if you choose to share your Workspace data through screen actions (including screenshots), some smart features in other Google products will still be available. An example is when you use screen actions to chat with Gemini Apps.

Learn how smart features use your Google Workspace content & activity

Important: By default, smart feature settings are off if you live in:

  • The European Economic Area
  • Japan
  • Switzerland
  • United Kingdom

When smart features are on, your data may be used to improve these features. Across Google and Workspace, we’ve long shared robust privacy commitments that outline how we protect user data and prioritize privacy. Generative AI doesn’t change these commitments — it actually reaffirms their importance. Learn how Gemini in Gmail, Chat, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides, Meet & Vids protects your data.

Change smart feature settings

Learn how to change your smart feature settings in different Google Workspace products. You can change smart feature settings on your computer or in the Gmail app for Android, iPhone, or iPad.

Change smart feature settings for Gmail, Chat & Meet

Important: Changes to smart feature settings apply across all devices and apps where you’re signed in.

  • If you’re on the mobile Gmail app but don’t get a notification about the changes, update your app.
  • Some changes made on your computer don’t reflect in the mobile app.
  1. On your computer, go to Gmail.
  2. At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  3. In the “General” tab, scroll to “Smart features.”
  4. Next to “Turn on smart features in Gmail, Chat, and Meet,” check or uncheck the box.
Change smart feature settings for Google Workspace & other Google products
Gmail
  1. On your computer, go to Gmail.
  2. At the top right, click Settings See all settings.
  3. Under the “General” tab, scroll to “Google Workspace smart features.”
  4. Click Manage Workspace smart feature settings.
  5. Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  6. At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Calendar
  1. On your computer, go to Calendar.
  2. At the top right, click Settings Settings.
  3. Under “General,” click Google Workspace smart features Manage Workspace smart features settings.
  4. Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  5. At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Chat
  1. On your computer, go to Chat.
  2. At the top right, click Settings Data Privacy.
  3. Under “Google Workspace smart features,” click Manage settings.
  4. Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  5. At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Drive
  1. On your computer, go to Drive.
  2. At the top right, click Settings Settings.
  3. Click Privacy.
  4. Click Manage Workspace smart feature settings.
  5. Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  6. At the bottom right, click Save.
Google Meet
  1. On your computer, go to Meet.
  2. At the top right, click Settings General.
  3. Next to “Google Workspace smart features,” click Manage.
  4. Turn a smart feature setting on or off:
    • Smart features in Google Workspace
    • Smart features in other Google products
  5. At the bottom right, click Save.

Learn how Google handles data in connection with smart feature settings

If you have a personal Google Account, this notice and our Privacy Policy describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

If you have a work or school Google Account, this notice and the Google Cloud Privacy Notice describe how Google handles your data in connection with these settings.

What are Google’s legal bases of processing for users in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland?

For users based in the European Economic Area, United Kingdom, or Switzerland, Google processes your information for the purposes, and on the legal grounds, described below.

When we refer to “your Workspace Content & Activity” below, we mean content from Workspace apps such as Calendar, Gmail, Chat, Meet, Drive, and more, and related data about how you use Workspace products.

Google’s legal bases are:

  • Your consent. We rely on your consent for Google to use your Workspace Content & Activity, when you turn on any of the smart features settings for Google Workspace, for the following purposes:
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in Gmail, Chat and Meet. For example, when you turn the smart features in Gmail, Chat and Meet setting on, you can get experiences that include Gmail Smart Compose (suggested text in email).
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience across Google Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in Google Workspace setting on, you can get experiences that include personalized search (such as keyword suggestions, file suggestions, and more relevant results). This setting does not affect your control over the smart features setting that personalizes your experience in Gmail, Chat, and Meet.
    • To provide smart features that personalize your experience in other Google products outside of Workspace. For example, when you turn the smart features in other Google products setting on, you can get experiences that include restaurant reservations and to-go orders in Maps. Data sharing and personalization in certain products may be subject to additional controls such Web and App Activity and DMA linked services (in the EU).
    You can revoke your consent to any of these purposes at any time by turning off the relevant setting as described in the “Change smart feature settings” section above.
  • Google and third parties’ legitimate interests with appropriate safeguards to protect your privacy.

    • To improve our services. If you have turned on any of the smart features settings, we may also process your Workspace Content & Activity to improve these features.

      Processing information for this purpose is necessary for the legitimate interests of Google and our users in:

      • Providing, maintaining and improving services for our users (such as a flight confirmation email you receive being used to create a summary card that appears in your Gmail).
      • Developing new products and features that are useful for our customers and users (for example, processing aggregated Gmail data helped us develop and launch Smart Compose suggestions as you enter text in Gmail).
      • Performing research that benefits our users and the public (such as to conduct a user study that helped us develop and launch Smart Reply suggested responses in Gmail).

      Learn more about how we’re protecting your Google Workspace data in the era of generative AI.

How long is your Workspace Content & Activity used to provide smart features and to improve these features?

Your Workspace Content & Activity is used to provide you with smart features as long as the relevant smart feature setting is turned on. Turning off a smart feature setting or deleting your Workspace Content & Activity stops that data from being used to provide relevant smart features to you in the future.

Turning off a smart feature setting means your Workspace Content & Activity will no longer be used to improve the relevant smart features moving forward. The learnings developed from this improvement process may persist even after you turn off a smart feature setting or delete your Workspace Content & Activity from your Google Account. However, turning off a smart feature setting means that your Workspace Content & Activity would no longer be actively processed to improve the relevant smart features after you have turned the setting off.

Search your Chrome history with Gemini in Chrome

Search your Chrome history with Gemini in Chrome

You can find pages you’ve visited before in Chrome by asking Gemini in Chrome. You don’t need to keep tabs open to save them for later, or remember the exact site and when you visited it. Just describe what you’re searching for using everyday language, like “what’s that chicken parmesan recipe I found last week?” Gemini in Chrome will search your Chrome history to help you rediscover that page and resume what you were doing.

What you need

This feature is only available if you:

  • Opted in to Gemini in Chrome. Learn how to get Gemini in Chrome.
  • Updated to the latest version of Chrome. Learn how to update Chrome.
  • Signed in to Chrome with a personal Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Chrome.
    • This feature isn’t available in Incognito mode. It’s also not available if you sign in to Chrome with a work or school Google Account.
  • Synced your Chrome history. Learn how to sync your history in Chrome.

Important: For now, this feature is not available in Live chats with Gemini in Chrome.

Find pages you visited in Chrome

  1. On your device, open Chrome.
  2. Select Ask Gemini .
  3. Ask Gemini in Chrome to find a page you previously visited.
    • Use everyday language to describe the page you’re trying to find.

Learn how to check or delete your Chrome browsing history.

Examples
  • Show me the article I was reading this morning about the stock market.
  • What was that place with vegan pizza I was looking at?
  • What was that hotel I was looking at in Palm Springs last week?
  • What were the steps for that DIY guide to fixing a leaky faucet?
  • Show me those ladies trousers I was looking at.

Gemini in Chrome can’t find the page

If you asked Gemini in Chrome to find a page you previously visited but it couldn’t find it:

  1. Make sure you’re signed in to the same Google Account you used when you visited the page. This should also be the same Google Account that you use with Gemini.
  2. If you use Chrome on multiple devices, check if your Chrome history is synced. Learn how to sync your history in Chrome.

How your data is handled

Learn more about what happens to your data when you use Gemini in Chrome.

Related resources

  • Use Gemini in Chrome
  • Go Live with Gemini in Chrome
  • Check or delete your Chrome browsing history

Share specific parts of your screen with Gemini in Chrome

Share specific parts of your screen with Gemini in Chrome

When you interact with Gemini in Chrome, you may want to focus on key details or points of reference, not the entire web page. You can use your cursor to highlight exactly what you want to ask about. The selected content is automatically attached to your Gemini prompt in Chrome. You can do things like…

  • Highlight a few pairs of sneakers and ask which is best for your running style.
  • Capture a part of a diagram or text for a clearer, more focused explanation.
  • Select a single object or part of a page to reimagine, redesign, or transform your idea.

What you need

You can select page content in Gemini in Chrome if:

  • You’re aged 13 and older and have access to Gemini in Chrome on desktop.
  • You are in one of the supported countries.
  • You can use this feature only on a Chromebook Plus, Mac, or Windows computer.

Select parts of your screen to share in your prompt

You can select parts of a webpage to include in your prompt so that Gemini understands the context of your question.

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
  3. In the panel, select Add menu .
  4. Click Select from screen.
  5. Draw boxes around specific parts of the web page that you want to ask about.
  6. In the text box, enter your question or request.

To exit Gemini in Chrome’s selection mode, press the Escape key.

Tip: Before you submit your prompt, you can adjust the size and position of your selected areas. Drag the edges or move the entire box.

Manage and remove selections

Adjust or remove a selection

To change the size or shape of your selection, hover your mouse over the corner and click and drag to make adjustments. You can also draw selections on top of each other if you want to make irregular shapes. If selected areas overlap, both are captured. If you selected content by mistake and want to cancel it, on the top right, click Close

Clear all selections from the tab

To remove selections from your prompt, in the side panel text box, hover over the selections and click Close . To remove all of your selections at once, close the Gemini in Chrome side panel.

Use Gemini in Chrome

Use Gemini in Chrome

With Gemini in Chrome, you can get AI assistance in your browser to easily get key takeaways, clarify concepts, find answers and more. To provide the most relevant responses, Gemini in Chrome uses content from your current browser tab. On a computer, you can also share up to 10 open tabs with Gemini.

What you need

Important: Gemini in Chrome is not available to all users at this time. We’re gradually releasing Gemini in Chrome, so it might not be available to you just yet.

To use Gemini in Chrome on your computer, you need to:

  • Be 13 or older (or the applicable age in your country) and in a supported region.
  • Use a Chromebook Plus, Mac, or Windows computer.
  • Use the latest version of Chrome. Learn how to update Chrome.
  • Sign in to Chrome. This feature isn’t available in Incognito mode. Learn how to sign in to Chrome.
  • Set your device settings to use a supported language.

If you are over 18 and use Gemini in Chrome with a work or school Google Account, access must be enabled by your administrator. Learn more about using Gemini Apps with a work or school Google Account.

Parents who choose to continue with supervision for children 13 or older (or the applicable age in their country) can turn off their child’s access to Gemini in Chrome using Family Link.

Chat with Gemini in Chrome

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top of your browser, click Ask Gemini .
    • You’ll need to opt in the first time you use Gemini in Chrome. To opt in, follow the onscreen instructions.
  3. In the text box, enter your question or request.
    • By default, Gemini in Chrome uses content from your current tab for its response. Learn how Gemini in Chrome works with your data.
      • Tabs opened from a chat or a shared tab are also shared with Gemini.
      • In Gemini Live, the current tab is shared by default, but you can share other tabs. Learn how to manage tabs in Gemini Live.
    • To add an open tab directly in your prompt, enter 0 and select the tab. You can also share up to 10 of your open tabs. Learn how to manage tabs shared with Gemini.

Tip: After you opt in to Gemini in Chrome , it’s added to your Mac menu bar or Windows system tray, and you can use keyboard shortcuts.

What you can do with Gemini in Chrome

After you opt in to Gemini in Chrome in the side panel, you can chat directly with Gemini. For example, try asking Gemini in Chrome to:

  • Summarize key takeaways from an article
  • Explain a complex topic in a different way
  • Help you test your knowledge of a new subject you’re learning
  • Modify a recipe to meet dietary needs
  • Compare or consolidate information across pages
  • Make recommendations based on your preferences
  • Complete multi-step actions on your behalf
  • Draft messages to send to others using Gmail
  • Look up your past photos and albums

Manage your chat with Gemini in Chrome

In Gemini in Chrome, you can:

  • Go Live & talk while you browse: at the bottom, click Live . Learn more about going Live with Gemini in Chrome.
    • Note: For users under 18, Live is not available.
  • Share or stop sharing a tab: in the text box, click Update tabs and select the tab you want to add or remove. A shared tab shows a Check mark .
  • Pop-out or dock Gemini in Chrome: at the top, click Pop-out chat or Dock to original tab .
  • Start a new chat: at the top, click Start new chat . If it’s not there, first click More options .
    • When you start a new chat, your current tab is shared with Gemini by default. To change this, you can turn off Share current tab by default in your Chrome settings. Learn how to turn it off in Chrome settings.
  • Switch between Gemini models: in the text box, click the model name , then select the model.
  • Find your recent Gemini chats: at the top, click More options .

Manage tabs shared with Gemini in Chrome

When you open Gemini in Chrome, the page content from your current tab is shared by default. Gemini uses that page content to respond. You can stop sharing your current tab at any time. Learn how Gemini in Chrome works with your data.

Stop sharing a tab

  1. In Gemini in Chrome, above the text box, click Show shared tabs .
  2. Next to the tab you want to stop sharing, click Remove tab .
    • When a tab is no longer shared, the glowing underline on the tab disappears.

Tip: If you start a new chat, your current tab is shared with Gemini by default. To change this, you can turn off Share current tab by default in your Chrome settings. Learn how to turn it off in Chrome settings.

Share a tab

In addition to your current tab, you can share up to 10 of your recent open tabs across your browser windows. Learn how Gemini in Chrome works with your data.

  1. At the top of your Chrome browser, click Ask Gemini .
  2. In the text box, click Add tabs .
  3. Select the tabs you want to add.
    • A shared tab shows a Check mark .
    • This shares the page content from the tabs you share, and Gemini uses it to respond.
    • When Gemini is using a page, its tab shows a glowing underline.

Tip: You can also search for and add open tabs by entering 0 and selecting the tab.

When you share a Workspace webpage

Gemini may directly access your Workspace account to respond to you about a Workspace webpage (like docs.google.com) that you shared in Chrome. This makes sure that Gemini can, for example, refer to an entire Google Doc you’ve asked about instead of only what’s available within the tab. To use more of your personal content from Workspace, connect the Workspace app. Learn how to connect Google Workspace apps & services to Gemini Apps.

Manage Gemini in Chrome settings

Hide or show Gemini icon on browser & desktop

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top, click More Settings.
  3. In the Settings menu, click AI innovations Gemini in Chrome .
    • If the menu is hidden, first click Menu .
  4. Under “Preferences,” turn the following settings on or off:
    • Show Gemini at the top of the browser
    • Show Gemini in Mac menu bar and turn on keyboard shortcut on Mac
    • Show Gemini in system tray and turn on keyboard shortcut on Windows

Tip: You can also right-click the top of your browser and click Unpin Gemini or Pin Gemini.

Manage permissions for Gemini in Chrome

  1. On your computer, open Chrome.
  2. At the top, click More Settings.
  3. In the Settings menu, click AI innovations Gemini in Chrome .
    • If the menu is hidden, first click Menu .
  4. Under “Permissions,” you can turn the following permissions on or off:
    • Precise location
    • Microphone
      • Users under 18 can’t turn on the Microphone or Closed Captions.
    • Share current tab by default
    • Let Gemini browse for you
      • ****Users under 18 can’t use auto browse.

Tip: If Precise location is on , Gemini in Chrome can access and use your precise location. If it’s off , Gemini in Chrome cannot access and use your precise location, and will only be able to derive an estimated location from your IP address.

Fix or report a problem & give feedback

If you can’t find or use Gemini in Chrome

Important: Gemini in Chrome is rolling out to users over time, so it may not be available in your country or territory yet.

If Gemini in Chrome is available in your country or territory, try these steps:

  1. Sign in to Chrome as an eligible user.
    • This feature isn’t available in Incognito mode or for Chrome profiles that are not signed-in. Learn how to sign in to Chrome.
    • To access Gemini in Chrome, you must be 13 or older (or the applicable age in your country). If you meet the minimum age requirement, you can verify your age. Learn more about age verification.
  2. Make sure you are in a supported country
    • Gemini in Chrome is available in select regions. If you are in a supported region but still can not use Gemini in Chrome, try the following steps:
      • Restart your browser and try again. If you recently traveled outside of these countries, your location may not have updated from your previous location.
      • Turn off your VPN. To do so, you often need to open the VPN app and select “Disconnect” or toggle a switch to “Off”.
    • If the issue remains after you try all of the above, update to the next version of Chrome when it is available and check if the problem is fixed.
  3. Ensure that Chrome browser is set up correctly:
    • Make sure you are using a Windows, Mac, Chromebook device which is set to a supported language.
    • Update your Chrome browser to the latest version. Learn how to update Chrome.
    • (Advanced) Try resetting your Chrome flags. Then, restart your browser.
  4. Other things to try If you still are having trouble accessing Gemini in Chrome, try the following steps:
    • Right-click the Gemini in Chrome side panel or floating chat box and select Reload.
    • Shut down virtualized environments: If you are accessing Chrome through a virtual machine, certain features may be restricted.
    • Check in with your system administrator: Make sure that use of Gemini in Chrome isn’t disabled by your organization.

Report a problem or send feedback about Gemini in Chrome

  1. At the top of Gemini in Chrome, click More Settings & help Send feedback.
  2. Enter a description of the problem or your feedback.
  3. Optionally, add a screenshot to help us better understand the issue.
  4. Click Send.

Learn more about how Google uses your feedback.

Report or give feedback on Gemini’s response

Your feedback helps make Gemini Apps more helpful, accurate, and safe.

To give feedback on a response:

  • Below Gemini’s response, click Good response or Bad response .
  • To report a legal issue, under Gemini’s response, click Report legal issue .

Learn more about how Google uses your feedback.

Use Gemini in Google Messages

Use Gemini in Google Messages

You can chat with Gemini in the Google Messages app to draft messages, brainstorm ideas, plan events, or simply have a fun conversation.

What you need

  • An Android phone.
  • Your phone’s language set to a supported language.
  • The latest version of Google Messages . Get it on Google Play.
  • A personal Google Account that you manage on your own.
    • You can’t use Gemini in Google Messages with a Google Account managed by Family Link or with a Google Workspace account.
  • Be 18 or over.
  • RCS chats turned on. Learn how to turn on RCS chats.

Supported languages for Gemini in Google Messages

Start a chat with Gemini in Google Messages

Important: Chats with Gemini aren’t end-to-end encrypted.

  1. On your Android phone, open Google Messages .
  2. Tap the chat with Gemini, or tap Start chat Gemini.
  3. For the first time, follow any on-screen instructions.
  4. Enter your question or prompt.
    • The first time you chat with Gemini, you can explore different conversations. Just tap a suggestion above the message field.
  5. Optionally, to add a photo to your prompt, tap Show attach media screen .
  6. Tap Send message .

Tip: You can also use apps in your chat with Gemini in Google Messages. Learn more about using apps with Gemini and how to manage apps in Gemini.

Examples
  • I haven’t reached out to my friend in a while. Help me draft a short message to check in and reconnect.
  • Suggest a 3-course dinner menu that’s impressive but manageable for a novice cook. Dietary restriction: vegetarian.
  • I’m going to a social event where I barely know anyone. Come up with a few interesting conversation starters.

Give feedback on a Gemini response

  1. Touch and hold the response you want to give feedback on.
  2. At the top, tap Good response or Bad response .

Report a legal issue

  1. Touch and hold a response.
  2. Tap More Report legal issue.

Report legal issue

Delete your Gemini chat

Important: In Google Messages, you can only delete your entire Gemini chat. In your Gemini Apps Activity, you can delete specific prompts from your Gemini chat.

In Google Messages

After you complete the steps below, your Gemini chat is deleted from your Gemini Apps Activity and Google Messages.

  1. In Messages, open your chat with Gemini.
  2. At the top, tap More Delete conversation.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions.

In Gemini Apps Activity

After you complete the steps below, your Gemini chat is deleted from your Gemini Apps Activity. It doesn’t delete the chat from Google Messages or any Android backup of your messages. To also delete it from Google Messages, follow the steps to delete the chat from Google Messages.

  1. Go to your Gemini Apps Activity.
  2. Next to a prompt or response in Google Messages, tap Delete activity item .
    • Activity from Google Messages shows a “ Google Messages” label.
  3. Follow the on-screen instructions.

Tip: To access your Gemini Apps activity from the Gemini web app, go to gemini.google.com. Then at the top, tap Menu Settings & help Activity.

What happens when you delete your Gemini chats

  • When you delete your Gemini chat in Google Messages or in your Gemini Apps Activity, Gemini can no longer access the chat.
  • When you delete your Gemini chat in Google Messages, it’s also deleted from your Gemini Apps Activity.
    • If the chat still shows in your Gemini Apps Activity or Google Messages on other devices, check the device you used to delete the chat. Make sure it’s connected to the internet and RCS chats are turned on. Learn how to turn on RCS chats.
  • When you delete your Gemini chat in your Gemini Apps Activity, it doesn’t delete it from Google Messages or any Android backup.
    • To also delete it from Google Messages, follow the steps to delete the chat from Google Messages.

Learn about your location data & Gemini in Google Messages

Gemini in Messages doesn’t have access to your precise location. It uses the general area from your IP address or the home or work addresses in your Google Account to give relevant responses to prompts like “What’s the weather?” Learn more about how Gemini in Messages estimates your general area.

Use Gemini Live on Android XR

Use Gemini Live on Android XR

On Android XR devices, you can chat naturally with Gemini Live as your personal AI companion. You can do things like:

  • Ask questions for a deeper understanding of what’s in your view.
  • Collaborate with Gemini across apps and windows on your screen.
Availability

You can use Gemini Live on the Android XR platform:

  • Where the Gemini mobile app is available
  • With a signed-in Google Account that you manage on your own

Chat with Gemini Live on your Android XR device

When you chat with Gemini on your Android XR device, you can explore more deeply. For example, you can ask Gemini questions about a complex video on YouTube, get help planning a trip while exploring the immersive view in Maps, or compare info across tabs in Chrome.

To chat with Gemini, on your Android XR Home screen, open Gemini  or say “Hey Google,” then ask a question to start a chat. You can also press and hold the top button on your Android XR device.

Note: When you start Gemini for the first time, follow the instructions to get started.

Chat live with Gemini

Gemini Live lets you have a natural back-and-forth conversation about the apps and windows on your screen.

To chat live with Gemini:

  1. On your Android XR device’s Home screen, select Gemini .
    • You can also go Live by saying “Hey Google” or by pressing and holding the top button.
  2. For your first time, follow any on-screen instructions.
  3. Start talking.
Share your view with Gemini Live

You can share your device’s view to get help from Gemini Live. When you choose to share your view, your full view is shared. If your virtual environment is off and view sharing is on, Gemini can access your space. Be careful with personal content like passwords, payment details, or medications, and ask for people’s permission before including them in your view.

To share your view with Gemini Live:

  1. On your Android XR device, open the Gemini mobile app .
  2. Select Turn on view sharing .
    • When you’re sharing your view, to stop sharing, select view sharing  again.
  3. Follow the on screen instructions.

You can also turn view sharing off in Gemini settings on your Android XR device. In Gemini settings, turn Enable view sharing in Live off . When Enable view sharing in Live is off, if you turn it on in Settings or select view sharing , you will be asked to consent again before you can share your view.

Privacy

Learn more about how Google handles your Gemini Live data in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub and the Gemini Apps Privacy Notice.

Android iPhone & iPad

Ask Gemini to handle your multi-step tasks in select Android apps

Ask Gemini to handle your multi-step tasks in select Android apps

You can ask the Gemini mobile app on Android to handle multi-step tasks for you in select apps on supported devices. Gemini uses screen automation, a beta feature in the Gemini mobile app, to help you with everyday tasks like booking rides, ordering food, and ordering groceries.

Tip: Screen automation is different from Gemini Agent and Connected Apps. Learn more about their differences.

What you need

To use Gemini to complete tasks in Android apps, you need to:

  • Have a supported Android device: Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, or Samsung Galaxy S26 Series.
  • Be 18 or over and in the US or Korea. Pixel 10 devices are not supported in Korea.
  • Be signed in with a personal Google Account. This feature isn’t available if you sign in to a work, school, or supervised Google Account. Learn how to sign in to Gemini Apps.

Important:

  • For now, screen automation is only available in English and for select apps.
  • This feature is only available in the Gemini mobile app on Android, including when you activate Gemini by touch or by saying “Hey Google.”
  • We’re gradually releasing this feature, so it might not be available to you just yet.

Before you use Gemini with screen automation

Gemini is still learning and can make mistakes, so avoid using screen automation for emergencies or tasks involving sensitive information. Do not enter sign-in info, payment details, or other sensitive info directly into the chat. Instead, if necessary to complete your action in an app, take control of the task and enter the details directly in the app. Also, keep in mind that Gemini can share information from your chat with Connected Apps. Learn more about Connected Apps.

Ask Gemini to complete tasks in your apps

  1. On your Android phone, open the Gemini mobile app .
    • You can also activate Gemini by touch or by saying “Hey Google.”
  2. Tell Gemini the details of the task you want it to complete in an app, like “Book a ride to the airport.”
    • If Gemini can complete a task using a connected app, it does that instead of using screen automation. If the app isn’t connected, you’ll get the option to connect it. Learn how to use and manage Connected Apps.
    • Gemini may ask for more details before it creates an action plan for your request.
    • Gemini works on the task in the background, even if you close the chat.
  3. For the first time Gemini uses screen automation, follow the on-screen instructions.
    • To complete tasks in apps for you, the Google app needs permission to use screen automation.
  4. If needed, review and confirm Gemini’s action plan for your task.
    • To make changes to the plan, submit a prompt that explains what you want updated.
  5. Follow the instructions in the chat to complete any steps that you need to complete and to complete the final step, like confirming a ride booking or placing an order.
    • If you ask Gemini to prepare an order but you don’t complete it, items may remain in your cart.
Examples
  • Book a ride:
    • Book a ride to the airport
    • Schedule a ride for tomorrow
  • Order food:
    • Reorder my last coffee
    • Order pizza for delivery
  • Order groceries:
    • Add milk and eggs to my grocery cart
    • Order groceries to my mom’s house

View, stop & take control of a task

Gemini completes tasks in apps using an on-device virtual phone environment. For example, it can open an app and interact with its screen, like adding an item to a cart for you. You can view Gemini’s progress live, and stop or take control of the task at any time. For certain tasks, Gemini will pause and ask you to take control.

To view and take control of a task:

  1. In the chat or live update notification, tap View progress.
    • This opens a view of the on-device virtual phone environment that Gemini is using to complete your task.
  2. To take control of the task, tap Take control.
  3. Complete your steps.

To stop the task:

  • In the chat text box, tap Stop response Stop task, or
  • In the live update notification, tap Stop task.

Manage permission to use screen automation

To complete tasks in apps for you, Google needs your permission to use screen automation. This permission allows Gemini to read and interact with other apps’ screen content. You can change this permission at any time.

  1. On your Android phone, open the Gemini mobile app .
  2. At the left, tap Menu  tap your Profile pic or initial Settings Screen automation.
  3. Select Always allow, Ask every time, or Do not allow.

Share a chat where Gemini used screen automation

Important:

  • Before you share a chat, review the public link and make sure it doesn’t include any private or sensitive info.
  • When you share a chat, a public link is created and anyone with the link can view it. Learn more about sharing chats from Gemini Apps.

You can share chats where Gemini used screen automation to complete tasks in Android apps. Learn how to share your chats.

Limits for screen automation in apps

There are limits on the number of:

  • Requests you can make where Gemini uses screen automation each day
  • Tasks Gemini can handle at the same time using screen automation

If you’re close to your limit, Gemini lets you know how many requests are left for the month. Learn more about limits in Gemini Apps.

How Gemini works with you to keep you & your info safe

Screen automation in Android apps is a beta feature. As we continuously work to improve the feature, please use it carefully to prevent unintended results. You’re responsible for Gemini’s actions during a task, including mistakes and unexpected results like purchases.

About possible risks of using AI agents

Agentic features, like screen automation in Gemini, are helpful and powerful tools, but it’s important to be aware of possible risks. Remember that Gemini can make mistakes and do unexpected things.

Gemini can make mistakes

Gemini might misunderstand what you want it to do or the app it’s interacting with. This could lead to unintended actions, like:

  • Following instructions incorrectly or tapping the wrong button or item
  • Completing a purchase or ordering something without your permission
  • Adding the wrong quantity of an item to your cart or forgetting to add an item
  • Confirming a task is done when it’s not or could have done more
  • Asking you to take over when it can normally do the step

Learn how to view, stop, and take control of a task.

About prompt injection

Prompt injection is an attempt to elicit an unintended or harmful response from generative AI tools like screen automation in Gemini. This happens when content, like a website, in-app content, an email, a document, or multimedia, has malicious instructions that might be hidden from you but visible to the AI agent.

If an AI agent reads these instructions while doing a task, it might be tricked into doing unintended things. For example, a malicious instruction could tell the agent to:

  • Place an order in the app without your confirmation
  • Change your delivery address or other information in an app
  • Send communications through chat functions in the app

Learn about how we address these risks in Gemini.

How screen automation is designed to keep you in control

  • “Take control” mode: Gemini may pause and ask you to “take control” of the task to complete specific actions, like:
    • Entering specific types of information (such as passwords or payment details)
    • Finalizing transactions
    • Signing in to an app
    • Creating an account
  • Requests for user confirmation: Gemini aims to ask for your review and confirmation before it completes certain actions in the app. For example:
    • Sending communications, like a message to your driver
    • Changing details, like your delivery address
  • Prohibited task recognition: Gemini has safeguards designed to help it recognize and not act on certain types of requests that could be harmful or are outside of its intended purpose, including tasks that may violate the Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy.
  • App & action restrictions: Gemini is designed to restrict its activity to the apps and actions relevant to your task. This helps protect your data on other unrelated apps and helps prevent actions that don’t align with your task.

Why monitoring your tasks is important & how to stop Gemini

Gemini’s safeguards for screen automation described above don’t guarantee protection against all risks.

Monitor your tasks

Monitoring your tasks is the most important way to protect against risk while Gemini uses screen automation. Review confirmation requests and clarifying questions closely. Use screen automation carefully and safely, and only give Gemini tasks you’re comfortable with. Be extra watchful when:

  • Gemini handles an important task
  • Gemini does anything where a mistake could be a problem
You’re in control

If Gemini is doing something you don’t like, you can view, stop, and take control of a task at any time. Learn how to view, stop, and take control of a task.

How your data is handled

Learn more about how your data is handled when Gemini uses screen automation.

About other features similar to screen automation

  • Gemini Agent: While screen automation only supports tasks in select Android mobile apps, you can use Gemini Agent for multi-step tasks in a live web browser if you’re eligible. Learn more about Gemini Agent.
  • Connected Apps: Screen automations and Connected Apps have their own settings. Also, screen automation won’t work on apps that are available as Connected Apps. If screen automation is off, you can still use Connected Apps. Learn more about Connected Apps.

  • Use & manage Connected Apps in Gemini

  • Android tablets, including Pixel Tablet

with 2 GB of RAM or more, running Android 9 and up.
